This includes a wide range of non-standard assumptions, some of them are highly relevant for practice such as generalized smoothness. In this paper proposes an approach of utilizing template solutions to derive guarantees in settings that do not admit an equivalent SDP formulation of exact worst-case performance problem. The approach is showcased by studying the performance of the gradient descent method for convex functions that also satisfy $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness assumption. Despite the inherent conservatism of the approach, this paper improves and generalizes an existing convergence guarantee to showcase the approach.
Optimization and Control.comment: This is the extended version of the paper Krivchenko, V. O. (2026). Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness. Doklady Mathematics, 530(1), 5-13. The extended version is much more detailed. It contains expanded discussion of the approach as well as descriptions of PEP experiments

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Weighted Volume Dissipativity and Sobolev Regularity at Limiting Rate
Optimization and Control.summary: Sharp pointwise divergence bounds for a nonlinear flow are studied under the requirement that the logarithm of the adapted positive density also be an exponentially decaying Lyapunov function. Invariant-measure duality supplies the unrestricted benchmark. Under two-sided quadratic Lyapunov bounds, scaling a prescribed Lyapunov function realizes every strictly suboptimal pointwise rate without reducing its decay rate, and the closure of the joint rate region is a rectangle. For a fixed reference volume form, the limiting pointwise rate has a smooth compatible certificate exactly when the differential of the reference divergence vanishes at the equilibrium. Otherwise, the infimal second-derivative supremum norm grows inversely with the gap to the limiting rate. Matching Sobolev cost bounds are proved in every finite dimension when the integrability exponent exceeds the dimension and the prescribed Lyapunov rate does not exceed half the baseline rate. The upper construction uses a regularized square root of the baseline Lyapunov function and keeps the potential and its gradient uniformly bounded. Matching contraction deficits under a Sobolev norm budget follow. A scalar borderline family has bounded second-derivative mass and a Lipschitz limit with atomic second derivative. The limiting exponent also holds in the reference measure with an explicit uniform volume prefactor, even when no smooth compatible instantaneous certificate exists. Scaling preserves the full baseline Lyapunov rate.

Optimization and Control.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to $O(N^{-4/3})$. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to $O(N^{-2/(3-κ)})$ and $O(N^{-4/(3-κ)})$, respectively, where $κ\in[0,1]$ describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.

Optimization and Control.title: Driver Surge Maps for Supply Rebalancing with Downstream Matching
Optimization and Control.summary: Ride-hailing platforms use driver-facing surge maps to rebalance spatial supply by offering zone-level bonuses. These bonuses can reshape supply by inducing nearby drivers to relocate and encouraging latent drivers to become dispatchable, but both responses are voluntary. Within short decision windows, platforms risk offering bonuses that reshape driver supply without generating sufficient downstream matching value to justify the associated payments. We formulate the driver surge map design problem (DSMDP) to optimize zone-level bonuses while anticipating voluntary driver responses and downstream matching. To assess how bonus adjustments affect net operating profit, we conduct a marginal analysis that identifies when small bonuses improve on the no-bonus map and how spatial smoothness links bonus decisions across zones. Using these marginal values, we develop an iterative solution approach (ISA) to sample dual sensitivities of the matching linear program across nearby matching regimes and guide real-time bonus updates. Theoretical analysis provides certificates of approximate stationarity and establishes conditions for stationary limits. Computational experiments show that ISA improves net operating profit over the best-performing feasible benchmark by up to 19.37% on the generated instances and by up to 8.43% in the New York City study. Local shortage alone is not a sufficient basis for bonus allocation. Platforms should target responsive supply whose downstream matching value justifies the associated bonus payments. Latent-driver activation can support higher-value matches even when all demand is served, but the resulting gains must also cover additional payments to drivers who would already be matched without incentives. Results indicate diminishing returns to bonus spending and show that moderate spatial smoothness can preserve most of the gains from spatial targeting.
Optimization and Control.comment: 49 pages, 4 figures, 12 tables, including a 16-page e-companion

Optimization and Control.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
Optimization and Control.summary: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\barσ_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. We construct these limits, among them the critical drum and the cake stand, a flat disk with a catenoidal horn. The families approach their limits like $j^{-1}$ for rings of $j$ caps, and the equatorial family approaches $4π$ with deficit $4πb^{-1}e^{-b}$. For large $b$, the leading terms of the multipole system reduce to the logarithmic energy of the cap centers and a formal evaluation gives $\barσ_1^\star(b)=8π-16π\,b^{-1}\log b+O(b^{-1})$.

Optimization and Control.title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $ε$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

Optimization and Control.title: Gradient Descent Achieves $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ Convergence
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent on a lower-bounded nonconvex function with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and Hessian. Classical analysis shows that a fixed stepsize guarantees a decrease of order $\varepsilon^2/L$ per update. In contrast, our rule uses a sequence of $\mathcal{O}(m)$ updates with a total stepsize of order $m^2/L$. We establish a weighted descent inequality for every prefix of the update sequence on a quadratic objective and control the error caused by Hessian variation on a general objective. This error determines the choice $m\asymp(L^2/(ρ\varepsilon))^{1/4}$ for small $\varepsilon$. We show that gradient descent with our stepsize rule finds an $\varepsilon$-stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ gradient evaluations, matching the optimal gradient-complexity guarantee.

Optimization and Control.title: Turnpike Estimates and Limiting Behavior for $N$-Player Differential Games under Displacement Monotonicity
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the long-time behavior of open-loop Nash equilibria of $N$-player stochastic differential games with nondegenerate idiosyncratic noise, under displacement monotonicity of the costs and joint strong convexity of the Lagrangians. We prove an exponential turnpike estimate: as the remaining horizon grows, the decoupling fields of the finite-horizon Pontryagin systems converge exponentially fast to the solution of a stationary Pontryagin system, which is unique in a natural stability class, and on bounded time intervals the equilibrium states and controls converge to those generated by this solution. The limiting control is a strong open-loop equilibrium of an associated ergodic $N$-player game, and the ergodic constant $λ^{i,N}$ of each player is the same at every such equilibrium. For the finite-horizon game, the law of the equilibrium state, at times away from the initial and terminal times, is exponentially close in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$ to the invariant measure of the limiting dynamics. Finally, the equilibrium cost of player $i$ on $[t,T]$ equals $(T-t)λ^{i,N}$ plus a uniquely determined corrector, up to an error exponentially small in $T-t$.

Optimization and Control.title: Parameter-Free Dynamic Regret under Heavy-Tailed Noise
Optimization and Control.summary: We study online convex optimization on a compact convex domain of diameter $D$ in which the learner observes, at each round, one stochastic subgradient and no loss values. The observations are conditionally unbiased, and the noise has an unconditional $p$-th moment at most $σ^p$ for an unknown $p\in(1,2]$; for $p<2$ its variance may be infinite. For a comparator sequence of path length $P_T$ we write $Λ_T=1+P_T/D$, and we show that the minimax expected dynamic regret is, up to numerical constants, \[ \min\Bigl\{GD\sqrt{TΛ_T}+σDT^{1/p}Λ_T^{(p-1)/p},\ GDT\Bigr\}, \] where $G$ bounds the subgradients. The lower bound holds on every compact convex domain of positive diameter. An algorithm that combines AdaGrad learners restarted at different frequencies through exponential weights with a data-dependent learning rate attains this rate for each fixed $p>1$, without knowing $G$, $σ$, $p$, or $P_T$: the constant of the first term is numerical, the constant of the second is $O(1+\log(p/(p-1)))$, and no logarithmic factor of $T$ appears. The analysis bounds the gradient energy separately on each restart block, which gives the exponent $(p-1)/p$ of $Λ_T$ in the noise term; a bound over the whole horizon gives the exponent $1/2$. Running the algorithm on epochs of doubling length removes the need to know $T$ at the cost of a factor $2+\sqrt2$. The appendices give a high-probability version and a synthetic study.

Optimization and Control.title: Constrained Online Learning with Noisy Constraint Values
Optimization and Control.summary: We study online convex optimization with time-varying constraints when the constraint values are observed only through noise. In each round the learner picks an action, pays a convex loss, and incurs a convex constraint value that should be nonpositive; it then receives unbiased estimates of the loss and constraint gradients, and an unbiased observation of the constraint value whose error has bounded variance. Performance is measured against the best fixed action in hindsight among those that satisfy every constraint, and violation by the largest total overspend over any interval of consecutive rounds, which we call budget violation. Our algorithm, LEDGER, has $O(\sqrt T)$ expected regret and $O(\sqrt{T\log T})$ expected budget violation over $T$ rounds, uses one projection per round, and needs no strictly feasible action. The logarithm cannot be removed: with Gaussian noise of fixed positive variance, every algorithm with $O(\sqrt T)$ worst-case regret has worst-case budget violation of order at least $\sqrt{T\log T}$, even if only the final total overspend is counted, and budget violation $O(\sqrt T)$ forces linear regret. When violation is instead the sum of the positive parts of the per-round constraint values (hard violation), no algorithm keeps both expected regret and expected hard violation sublinear if the noise distribution is not fixed, even for affine constraints. With a fixed and known Gaussian noise law of standard deviation $σ$, a worst-case lower bound of order $\min\{σ,1\}T(\log\log T/\log T)^2$ shows that regret and hard violation cannot both be made polynomially sublinear. Noisy constraint values therefore still allow a signed budget to be controlled, at the cost of a logarithmic factor, but not the hard violation.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal control of SDEs with merely measurable drift: an HJB approach
Optimization and Control.summary:
We investigate an optimal control problem for a diffusion whose drift and running cost are merely measurable in the state variable. Such low regularity rules out the use of Pontryagin's maximum principle and also invalidates the standard proof of the Bellman principle of optimality. We address these difficulties by analyzing the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Working in a weak formulation of admissible controls, we first establish the state-equation solvability and Krylov estimates needed to make the control problem well defined. Using PDE techniques together with a policy iteration scheme, we prove that the HJB equation admits a unique strong solution, and this solution coincides with the value function of the control problem. Based on this identification, we establish a verification theorem and recover the Bellman optimality principle without imposing any additional smoothness assumptions.
  We further investigate a mollification scheme depending on a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$. It turns out that the smoothed value functions $V_{\varepsilon}$ may fail to converge to the original value function $V$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, and we provide an explicit counterexample. To resolve this, we identify a structural condition on the control set. When the control set is countable, convergence $V_{\varepsilon} \to V$ holds locally uniformly.

Optimization and Control.title: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
Optimization and Control.summary:
The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data.
  Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.

Optimization and Control.title: Uniform symmetric spectral finiteness of cones definable in o-minimal structures
Optimization and Control.summary: Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined by a complementarity problem over a closed convex cone. We show that every closed convex cone that is definable in an o-minimal structure is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite; that is, the cone spectra of symmetric matrices relative to the cone (the sets of their cone-constrained eigenvalues) have uniformly bounded cardinality. In particular, we derive explicit uniform bounds for semialgebraic cones, and the explicit uniform bound we obtain for a Löwner cone depends only on the order of the matrices in the cone. Using the uniform finiteness of cone spectra, we also show that the number of singular values relative to two closed convex cones definable in a common o-minimal structure is uniformly bounded. Finally, we provide a closed convex cone that is not definable in any o-minimal structure and for which the spectra of symmetric matrices are finite but have no uniform cardinality bound.

Optimization and Control.title: Robust Estimators for Stochastic Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) methods are popular for solving stochastic optimization problems, with model-based methods being a practically successful class of DFO algorithm. In most existing works, sufficiently accurate objective estimates (used for model construction and to test for sufficient decrease) are constructed by taking a sample mean of several noisy evaluations. In this work, we demonstrate that using robust estimators (specifically the median, trimmed mean, and median-of-means) can improve the sample complexity of model-based DFO methods. Our numerical results demonstrate that robust estimators are also a practical choice for algorithm implementations.

Optimization and Control.title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

Optimization and Control.title: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
Optimization and Control.summary: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, stable log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out consecutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.

Optimization and Control.title: A Sequential Quadratic Programming Perspective on Optimal Control
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper investigates the relationship between the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR), Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), and Newton's method for optimal control problems. Using a unified Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework, we introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based algorithm that solves for the exact Newton step the optimal control problem. Within this framework, we establish that iLQR is a principled modified SQP method rather than merely an approximation of DDP. We show that iLQR generates a descent direction, whereas the inclusion of dynamics Hessians in DDP and Newton-LQR may lead to indefinite quadratic subproblems and necessitate regularization. We further distinguish DDP and the proposed Newton-LQR algorithm through their treatment of costate information and second-order dynamics terms. Numerical experiments across six benchmark problems demonstrate that iLQR often exhibits superior convergence during the initial optimization phase, while Newton-LQR and DDP can exploit second-order information to accelerate convergence near a solution.

Optimization and Control.title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz under Pointwise Commutation
Optimization and Control.summary: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic convergence of the corresponding sparse moment--SOS hierarchy for polynomial matrix optimization. We also derive a criterion for finite convergence of moment relaxation and extraction of a global minimizer based on local flatness and consistency of the local representing matrix measures on overlapping variable blocks. Finally, we provide a sufficient construction of commuting decompositions through linear equations, using a reference polynomial matrix with a simple spectrum at some point.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonlinear Estimation with Convex Models
Optimization and Control.summary: A linear functional of an object from a convex symmetric set can be optimally estimated, in a worst-case sense, by a linear functional of observations made on the object. This well-known fact is extended here to a nonlinear setting: other simple functionals of the object can be optimally estimated by functionals of the observations that share a similar simple structure. This is established for the maximum of several linear functionals and even for the $\ell$th largest among them. Proving the latter requires an unusual variation of the analytical Hahn--Banach theorem. The existence results are accompanied by practical recipes relying on convex optimization to construct the desired functionals, thereby justifying the term of estimation algorithms.

Optimization and Control.title: Bounds on the Distance of Subgradient Trajectories to the Optimal Set
Optimization and Control.summary: A subgradient method with a constant step size may reach a minimizer and subsequently move away from it. Thus, a bound on the best objective value does not characterize the remainder of the trajectory. In this manuscript, we first establish that the trajectory enters a near-optimal sublevel set in finitely many iterations. We then use the Hausdorff distance between this sublevel set and the optimal set to bound the distance of every subsequent iterate from the optimal set. For objectives with weak sharp minima, we derive a tighter bound and construct examples demonstrating that the bound is tight. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results and illustrate when the bounds are conservative.

Optimization and Control.title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
Optimization and Control.summary: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations. For two arrivals with binary valuations and every $k\ge2$, the optimal fraction is $1/p$, where $p$ is the largest integer with $1+\binom{2p}{2}\le k$. In particular, up to six binary types permit full maximin share. For two arbitrary additive types, a different polynomial-time algorithm guarantees $4/7$ of maximin share for any number of agents. This ratio is tight for the algorithm. With three arrivals and two types, the optimal deterministic fraction is exactly $9/10$. For randomized policies with $k$ known additive types, the optimal MMS fraction guaranteed to all agents with probability at least $1-δ$ on every fixed arrival sequence is $Θ(\max\{k^{-1/2},\sqrtδ\})$ for $0\leδ<1$.

Optimization and Control.title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program
Optimization and Control.summary: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.

Optimization and Control.title: Splitting Compositions of Monotone Operators
Optimization and Control.summary:
Coupled convex optimisation equilibria and nonlinear circuits lead to inclusions of the form $0 \in Hx + A(Bx) - b$, where $A$ and $B$ are maximally monotone but the complete operator need not be monotone. We develop a one-parameter family of triangular warped-resolvent algorithms on product Hilbert spaces to solve such inclusions. Introducing $y \in Bx$ exposes a directed lift, and a composition-adapted kernel organizes each iteration into one evaluation of $H$ and one ordinary resolvent evaluation per factor block.
  A nonnegative multi-block gain matrix certifies a unique lifted solution, global linear convergence, and residual error bounds. An exact Schur reduction converts the $2n \times 2n$ condition into an equivalent $n \times n$ criterion. For nonpositive extrapolation, this criterion is necessary and sufficient to guarantee a unique fixed point and global linear convergence for all problems satisfying the given gain bounds. Minimum-gain estimates characterize its exact finite-stepsize feasibility boundary. A negative-coupling rotation family exhibits certified convergence when neither the original operator nor its specified lift admits a fixed positive-definite monotonicity metric. For a nonlinear periodic RLC circuit, we establish continuous-time nonmonotonicity and derive a computable convergence certificate. Our algorithm is demonstrated on a periodic circuit simulation problem.
Optimization and Control.comment: 23 pages, 4 figures. Revised manuscript with new multiport convergence results, a minimum-gain analysis of stepsize feasibility, and a nonlinear RLC circuit application

Optimization and Control.title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
Optimization and Control.summary: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. We then show how to improve the bound to $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-1})$. Here $δ_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

Optimization and Control.title: On the Impact of Alternative Settlement Rules for State-of-Charge-Limited Resources in Electricity Markets
Optimization and Control.summary: Standard two-settlement markets compute a participant's total profit as the sum of its day-ahead (DA) profit and its incremental real-time (RT) profit. This rule was designed for conventional generators, which can always deliver their DA schedules in RT because their capacity is the same in both markets. Energy storage resources, in contrast, are limited by their state of charge (SOC), so their ability to honor a DA award depends on the SOC available at the time of RT dispatch. When this SOC is insufficient, the RT market may impose a buy-back or sell-back that can lead to a monetary loss. This paper formalizes this asymmetry between SOC-unlimited and SOC-limited resources and assesses three alternative settlement rules: a zero-profit floor; a max rule, which pays storage the maximum of its RT-only profit and its standard DA plus incremental RT profit; and a variant of the max rule applied only when the standard profit is negative. Through our analysis and a case study based on a realistic version of the California system, we identify when storage is most exposed to losses, assess how the alternative rules let storage deviate from DA awards to provide flexibility, and quantify their impact on revenue adequacy.

Optimization and Control.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approximations introduce for statistical inference, we adopt a random-scaling approach that eliminates the need for explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix. We establish the asymptotic normality of the averaged primal--dual iterates and construct a self-normalized statistic that is asymptotically pivotal. The resulting inference procedure is fully online, requires neither covariance estimation nor matrix inversion, and incurs an additional per-iteration cost of the same order as that of the optimization update. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of both optimization performance and statistical inference accuracy.

Optimization and Control.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
Optimization and Control.summary: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

Optimization and Control.title: Sampling Error in Time-Discretized Stochastic Optimal Control
Optimization and Control.summary: We study sampling error for Euler discretizations of stochastic optimal control problems driven by Brownian motion. For ordinary Monte Carlo sampling, the error can diverge under time refinement when empirical-mean fluctuations accumulate as bias. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and a bounded noise coefficient, we derive finite-sample bounds for the value-function error without assuming smooth value functions or independence across sampling batches. The bounds isolate the empirical-mean contribution. For convergence under time refinement, ordinary Monte Carlo generally requires the number of samples per stage to grow at a faster rate than the number of intervals in the time mesh, whereas antithetic and recentered sampling eliminate the empirical-mean term and yield error bounds uniform over meshes with a fixed sample size per stage. We establish lower bounds showing that the ordinary and antithetic sampling terms are attained. We also prove sample-size convergence for all three methods on fixed meshes. For antithetic and recentered sampling, convergence is uniform over meshes in every noise dimension, with sharp sample-size rates in dimensions at least three.

Optimization and Control.title: Service location flexibility in dynamic vehicle routing
Optimization and Control.summary: Parcel lockers and delivery robots let a vehicle serve customers at nearby locations. We study this service location flexibility in the dynamic traveling repairman problem, where a single vehicle may serve each demand anywhere within a radius $r$ of its location. Arrivals form a Poisson process, demand locations are independent and uniform in the unit square, and on-site service times are i.i.d. with uniformly bounded second moments, where the radius $r$ may vary across systems as the on-site load $ρ$ tends to one. In this heavy-traffic regime, the optimal mean system time is of order $(1-ρ)^{-1}(1+\min\{1/r,1/(1-ρ)\})$, compared with $(1-ρ)^{-2}$ without service location flexibility [BvR91, PFB11]. Thus, flexibility reduces the order of optimal mean system time when $r$ stays fixed or shrinks more slowly than $1-ρ$. Moreover, when $r$ is on the order of $1-ρ$ or larger, the vehicle can attain the optimal order by repeating a fixed covering route that passes within $r$ of every location. For example, the vehicle can follow a fixed grid route through parcel lockers, with customers in each square cell sharing the locker at its center.

Optimization and Control.title: An augmented generalized factorization bound for generalized maximum-entropy sampling
Optimization and Control.summary: Li proposed an augmented factorization upper bound for use in branch-and-bound (B&B) algorithms aimed at the maximum entropy sampling problem (MESP). This bound improves on the factorization bound for MESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. GMESP, which selects $s$ of $n$ variables so as to maximize the product of the $t$ greatest eigenvalues of the corresponding principal submatrix of the covariance matrix, is a generalization of MESP (the case $t=s$), and the factorization bound for MESP generalizes to GMESP. We extend the augmentation technique of Li to improve on the generalized factorization bound for GMESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. We derive fundamental properties of the augmented bound, and we develop primal--dual constructions for use within B&B. We give checkable conditions under which the relaxation can be solved in closed form, which always hold when $t=1$, at the root and at every subproblem, and a condition under which the closed-form solution is optimal for GMESP. We compare the augmented bound with the spectral bound, establishing an exact comparison for $t=1$, an improved worst-case comparison for general $t$, and sufficient conditions for the dominance of each bound over the other. Computational experiments on benchmark instances show that augmentation can substantially reduce root gaps of the generalized factorization bound, while even reducing its computational time, and that it improves the performance of B&B. Moreover, a hybrid strategy that uses the trace upper bound to prune nodes and the closed-form certificate to avoid solving the relaxation can significantly accelerate B&B when $t$ is small.

Optimization and Control.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Time-Invariant Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper presents a tractable tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme that uses only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system. A simplex constraint is imposed on the Hankel coefficient vector, yielding explicit polyhedral bounds on the prediction mismatch induced by bounded measurement noise. Using certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets, we derive a tube-tightened formulation whose online optimization problem is a strictly convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input and state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability of the closed loop with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance of the proposed method.

Optimization and Control.title: An $O(n^{-1/2})$ remainder for the Chow--Robbins stopping boundary
Optimization and Control.summary: We sharpen the asymptotic approximation to the optimal stopping boundary in the Chow--Robbins game, proving the inverse-square-root remainder conjectured by Elton. The proof combines an exactly harmonic integral for simple random walk with a Catalan first-passage renewal identity. Averaging the stopping defect over one spatial period removes its leading lattice dependence, and a coupling of states at equal depth transfers this cancellation to the renewal sum. Consequently, the explicit integer stopping rule can fail at no more than a constant times the square root of the number of observation times.

Optimization and Control.title: Adaptive Robust Optimisation for Frequency-Constrained Market Clearing Problem
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper formulates the day-ahead market clearing as a two-stage adaptive robust optimisation problem in which the first stage determines unit commitment, energy dispatch, and reserve procurement, while the second stage represents worst-case balancing actions under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation, load, and HVDC converter outages. Frequency security is enforced explicitly through inertia and fast frequency response constraints at the synchronous-area level, with HVDC lines allowed to provide emergency power support within their available headroom. The resulting min--max--min problem is solved by a column-and-constraint generation algorithm and applied to an eight-country North Sea test system comprising three synchronous areas, sixteen onshore bidding zones, and five offshore wind farm hubs connected through a meshed HVDC grid. We compare the Home Market (HM) and Offshore Bidding Zone (OBZ) designs on this infrastructure across different uncertainty scenarios. The results first demonstrate the value of robustness, where deterministic solutions that ignore uncertainty are severely vulnerable to worst-case realisations. Comparing the two designs, we find that OBZ's offshore zone boundaries make line congestion visible to the day-ahead market, enabling targeted reserve procurement that raises day-ahead costs but substantially reduces real-time load shedding, yielding a net reduction in total system cost that grows with the severity of localised offshore uncertainty. When both designs face the identical worst-case contingency, HM cannot distinguish an offshore converter trip from normal operation and thus fails to hedge against it, while OBZ considers the risk at the day-ahead stage. This advantage can be seasonal, scaling with the ratio of offshore wind output to HVDC line capacity and diminishing when onshore generation dominates the supply mix.

Optimization and Control.title: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study how the choice of harvest quadrature affects optimal control in a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. With harvesting alone, counting the prey removed at each step gives a strictly convex cost. Using the prey density at the start of the step overestimates the catch and can create a strict local minimum with cost above the global minimum. We certify the global minimizers in a two-step example by rational root isolation. A second example shows that, with both species present and positive diffusion, a strict local minimizer for the old-state rule admits a descent direction under the flux rule.
  For nonnegative $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities in one space dimension, the two rules give costs, weighted gradients and Hessians that differ by $O(τ)$ at the same control, uniformly in the spatial mesh. Here $τ$ is the time step. If the old-state Hessian is uniformly coercive near a stationary control, the flux objective has a local minimizer within $O(τ)$ of it. With uniformly bounded tracking targets, a large enough effort penalty makes both objectives strongly convex for all sufficiently small time steps. We also derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions, prove a common variational limit with an IMEX discretization, and compare stationary controls across grids. The same harvest accounting applies to weighted production--destruction systems.

Optimization and Control.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. Efficient variations, including parallel Jacobi updates within each agent's subproblem and single-step constraint linearization, further reduce computation. Experiments on 2D and 3D tasks with up to 1024 agents demonstrate improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over state-of-the-art derivative-based distributed optimization, and superior scalability to existing distributed sampling methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Distributed Time-Varying Resource Allocation in Open Networks
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the problem of distributed resource allocation over a team of agents whose active membership changes over time. Each agent's allocation evolves according to its own temporal dynamics, while a shared equality constraint couples all active agents at every instant. For the case of quadratic local objectives, we show that the optimal solution is characterized by a linear system whose coefficient matrix couples a block-tridiagonal temporal structure with a block-diagonal Laplacian capturing the time-varying communication graph. Building on this structure, we develop a distributed forward-backward sweeping algorithm in which each agent resolves its own temporal coupling through a local forward-backward sweep, while the shared resource constraint is resolved through a distributed consensus iteration that is feasible at every iteration. Under a mild diagonal-dominance condition on the temporal coupling, we establish that the optimal allocation at any fixed time converges geometrically to a stationary solution as the horizon grows, and that our distributed algorithm tracks this limit at a matching geometric rate. These results justify a memory-efficient variant of the algorithm in which each agent retains only a bounded window of past history, with the resulting approximation error decaying exponentially in the window size. We validate these theoretical guarantees through numerical simulation, confirming the predicted convergence rates under dynamically changing team membership.

Optimization and Control.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stability are established. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

Optimization and Control.title: Randomized Forward Mode of Automatic Differentiation For Optimization Algorithms
Optimization and Control.summary: Reverse mode automatic differentiation (AD) computes a gradient in a single sweep, but at a memory cost that grows with the length of the computational graph. That cost becomes the binding constraint when the graph is long, as in parameter identification governed by differential equations or in training on memory-limited hardware. We study a randomized forward mode gradient (RFG) as an alternative to backpropagation in precisely this regime. RFG is a random gradient estimator built from the directional derivative along a random vector, a quantity that forward mode AD computes without storing a tape. Replacing the gradient with RFG yields a class of optimization algorithms; for RFG-based gradient descent (GD) and Polyak's heavy ball (PHB) methods, we establish convergence results on quadratic functions. The analysis reveals that using random vectors from a probability distribution with the smallest kurtosis yields the fastest rate of convergence. Computational experiments demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithms and verify the theoretical findings, including beyond quadratic functions. We further characterize when RFG is computationally preferable to backpropagation. Since the variance of RFG grows with the parameter dimension $d$ while the memory required by the reverse mode grows with the length $\ell$ of the computational graph, the relevant figure of merit is the ratio $\ell/d$. We confirm this by measurement against reverse mode with checkpointing. For a physics-informed neural network, where $d$ is large and $\ell$ short, RFG is not competitive. For parameter identification governed by differential equations, where a handful of coefficients is recovered from a long time integration, RFG requires one to three orders of magnitude less memory. The price is a larger iteration count, which leaves its time to solution comparable to or worse than a well-tuned reverse mode.

Optimization and Control.title: Minimal Control Time of Large Generic Quantum Systems at Critical Spectral Growth
Optimization and Control.summary: The minimal time needed to steer a closed quantum system between two arbitrary states is a fundamental performance limit of quantum control. For single-input bilinear Schrödinger systems of dimension $d$ with unbounded controls, this state-to-state control time is bounded from above by the weight $M_d$ of a minimum spanning tree (MST) built from the drift Hamiltonian written in the eigenbasis of the control Hamiltonian. We ask whether the control time of a \emph{generic} system, whose control Hamiltonian has a Haar-distributed eigenbasis, vanishes as $d\to\infty$ in the critical regime of drift eigenvalues growing as $k^{3/2}$. We prove that the finite clusters of the interaction matrix are asymptotically independent Gaussians, analyse the resulting independent surrogate model, for which $M_d \asymp (\ln d)^{-1/2}$ with an explicit finite-size expansion predicting $M_d\sqrt{\ln d}\to 10/3$, and test the exact Haar model by Monte Carlo simulations up to $d=18101$. The exact and surrogate models are statistically indistinguishable in mean at all tested dimensions, and both are consistent with the predicted limit, supporting the conjecture that the control time vanishes, albeit only logarithmically.
Optimization and Control.comment: Major rewrite: control-theoretic reframing; mathematical content essentially unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Extended Set-based Tasks for Multi-task Execution and Prioritization
Optimization and Control.summary: The ability of executing multiple tasks simultaneously is an important feature of redundant robotic systems. As a matter of fact, complex behaviors can often be obtained as a result of the execution of several tasks. Moreover, in safety-critical applications, tasks designed to ensure the safety of the robot and its surroundings have to be executed along with other nominal tasks. In such cases, it is also important to prioritize the former over the latter. In this paper, we formalize the definition of extended set-based tasks, i.e., tasks which can be executed by rendering subsets of the task space asymptotically stable or forward invariant using control barrier functions. We propose a formal mathematical representation of such tasks that allows for the execution of more complex and time-varying prioritized stacks of tasks using kinematic and dynamic robot models alike. We present an optimization-based framework which is computationally efficient, accounts for input bounds, and allows for the stable execution of time-varying prioritized stacks of extended set-based tasks. The proposed framework is validated using extensive simulations, quantitative comparisons to the state-of-the-art hierarchical quadratic programming, and experiments with robotic manipulators.

Optimization and Control.title: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence
Optimization and Control.summary: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater influence on the dynamics of the system than predicted by a Lindblad-type equation that models decoherence as time- and control-independent.

Optimization and Control.title: Transformers with Signatures: Towards Universal In-Context Learning in Path Space
Optimization and Control.summary:
In-context learning (ICL) enables transformers to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations without updating their parameters. However, theoretical guarantees for transformers remain limited in general, and elusive in particular when target responses depend nonlinearly on the evolution of observed paths. We establish an ICL framework for path space, using path signature features. Building on the universal linear approximation property of signatures, we construct explicitly a causal softmax transformer with two attention heads per layer that emulates in-context Lasso. Under sparse signature approximation and suitable moment and concentration conditions, we establish finite-sample prediction error bounds. Our analysis goes beyond the IID data setting in the existing ICL theory, allowing dependence among demonstrations and the query.
  Experiments on in-context sparse recovery, nonlinear path regression, execution-cost prediction, and financial payoff inference demonstrate robustness to changes in observation grids and adaptation to unseen market environments. Across these prediction tasks, transformers with signatures match or outperform vanilla transformer baselines with substantially fewer trainable parameters, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of signature-based ICL.

Optimization and Control.title: Using delays for prescribed-time static output feedback stabilization of LTI controllable and observable systems
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper addresses a stabilization problem: can every controllable and observable LTI system be stabilized by static output feedback (SOF)? To the best of our knowledge, we provide, for the first time, a solution to this problem. Furthermore, the proposed design achieves prescribed-time convergence to the origin independently of the initial condition. Two SOF methods are developed. The first employs multiple artificial discrete output delays with smooth time-varying gains and provides an explicit gain construction for every controllable and observable LTI system, based on a generalized controllability--observability Gramian introduced in this paper. The second combines constant-gain feedback of the current output with time-varying-gain feedback of a single artificially delayed output and also applies to every controllable and observable LTI system. Its simpler structure requires auxiliary parameters whose existence is guaranteed but whose explicit construction is provided only for SISO systems. The multiple-delay design is further extended to known bounded and fast-varying (without any constraints on the delay derivative) measurement delays that may be large, yielding fixed-time stabilization under a corresponding rank condition, with an assignable settling-time bound greater than three times the delay bound. For practical implementation, we further present an SOF controller with time-varying gains that depends on discrete-time delayed measurements. For unknown constant measurement or input delays, fixed-time stabilization is established for systems with nilpotent state matrices. A numerical implementation of Gramian-based gains is also suggested. Numerical examples involving nonminimum-phase, flexible-structure, and cart--pole systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
Optimization and Control.summary: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $κ$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $Ω\left(κ^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1δ\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<δ<1$ and sufficiently large $κ$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $κ$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

Optimization and Control.title: The uncertainty of a tournament draw: Insights from the Champions League
Optimization and Control.summary: The group draw of major sports tournaments implies some uncertainty, with lucky teams often enjoying a substantial unfair advantage. For the first time in the literature, we propose a technique to quantify this draw uncertainty, which, arguably, should be minimised. Our simulation-based approach requires generating a representative set of random draws to compute the variance of qualifying probabilities for each team. The method is applied to compare draw uncertainty in the former group stage and the current incomplete round-robin league phase of the UEFA Champions League, under both accurate and inaccurate seedings. We also break down the impact of the 2024/25 reform into various components. The new format is found to decrease draw uncertainty, but the reduction is mainly attributable to the inaccurate seeding system used by UEFA. Consequently, the primary benefit of an incomplete round-robin tournament compared to the standard group stage lies in the robustness of its draw uncertainty to the seeding of the teams.

Optimization and Control.title: A Unified View of Operator Splitting and Interior-Point Methods
Optimization and Control.summary: First-order splitting and interior-point methods offer contrasting computational trade-offs for convex conic quadratic programs, yet their linear systems look remarkably similar. We make this connection precise through the Moreau slack, an unconstrained variable from which multipliers and (ordinary) slacks satisfying exact or barrier-perturbed complementarity are recovered. The remaining feasibility equations define a unified residual whose roots are KKT points at zero barrier parameter and central-path points at positive barrier parameter. Applying splitting to this residual yields projection methods at zero barrier parameter and barrier splitting at positive parameter; Newton's method in the latter setting gives an implicit interior-point method. At fixed positive barrier parameter, matching the splitting metric to current barrier curvature equalises the primal variable corrections under the same regularisation and leaves a factor of two between the Moreau-slack corrections. With metrics frozen at a barrier solution, local analysis identifies when doubling improves (local) convergence and when the primal solve remains the bottleneck. Metric choices that simplify linear solves (eg make them diagonal) become Newton regularisations, exposing a shared convergence cost associated with computational convenience. Finally, a computable defect in the regularised Newton equations gives an accuracy-based criterion for reusing a splitting factorisation.

Optimization and Control.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
Optimization and Control.summary: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.

Optimization and Control.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. A neural network predicts distributed energy resource (DER) setpoints conditioned on operating conditions, switch configurations, and objective weights. The predicted setpoints are then processed through a DER projection and differentiable AC power flow to enforce device limits and network equalities. The framework is trained by directly minimizing the AC-OPF objective, without optimal-solution labels. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems yield mean objective gaps of 0.32%, 0.92%, and 0.56%, respectively, relative to IPOPT, across wide operating ranges. Across these systems and the evaluated high-load/low-generation and low-load/high-generation scenarios, the largest mean gap is 1.04%, with mean speedups of 58-5272 times relative to IPOPT.

Optimization and Control.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
Optimization and Control.summary: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.

Optimization and Control.title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
Optimization and Control.summary: Organizations use large language models (LLMs) to classify jobs that differ in uncertainty and the cost of errors. Querying additional models may improve accuracy, but it also incurs fees and increases congestion at shared servers. We study congestion-aware adaptive routing (CAAR) policies that adapt model selection and stopping decisions to observed outputs while accounting for the steady-state congestion they generate. The objective is to minimize the long-run average cost of misclassification penalties, query fees, and holding costs. We can represent CAAR policies as a mixture of decision trees, and derive exact holding costs for first-come-first-served servers with exponential service times and processor-sharing servers with general service times. We formulate a convex optimization problem with unique optimal model loads. Congestion prices capture the marginal system-wide holding costs of additional queries and guide routing and stopping decisions through a Bayesian dynamic program. We characterize optimal stopping decisions and identify models whose information does not justify their cost. A column-generation algorithm computes optimal CAAR policies and provides an explicit optimality-gap bound. We also bound the additional cost of limiting cascade depth relative to full-depth CAAR. Finally, under a common query-depth limit, cascades with a predetermined model order can be arbitrarily more costly than optimal CAAR, even when the order is randomized and stopping decisions adapt to observed outputs. Numerical experiments distinguish the benefits of adaptive model selection and congestion-aware design.

Optimization and Control.title: Connected Lie groups with a left-invariant intrinsic chronometer
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we investigate left-invariant intrinsic chronometers (time functions) on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups. We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. A one-to-one correspondence is established between chronometers satisfying the proposed system of axioms (including upper semi-continuity and the condition that the interiors of chronological rhombi form a base for the topology) and smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures. It is shown that an axiomatic chronometer uniquely determines a closed, pointed, convex cone in the Lie algebra, whose linear span satisfies the Chow--Rashevskii condition, and an upper semi-continuous concave positively homogeneous anti-norm on it. Conversely, it is proved that any such algebraic structure satisfying a local chronologicity condition induces an intrinsic chronometer with the required properties. The proofs rely on local estimates in exponential coordinates, the Hahn--Banach separation theorem, and properties of weak limits in optimal control problems.

Optimization and Control.title: From Inexact Gradients to Byzantine Robustness: Acceleration and Optimization under Similarity
Optimization and Control.summary:
Distributed learning algorithms are vulnerable to adversarial nodes, a.k.a. Byzantine failures. To solve this issue, robust algorithms have been developed, which typically replace parameter averaging with robust aggregations. While generic conditions on these aggregations exist to guarantee the convergence of (Stochastic) Gradient Descent (SGD), the analyses remain rather ad hoc. This hinders the development of more complex robust algorithms, such as accelerated ones. In this work, we show that Byzantine-robust distributed optimization can, under standard generic assumptions, be cast as a general optimization with inexact gradient oracles, an active field of research. This allows us to obtain state-of-the-art results for Byzantine-robust optimization from general inexact first-order analyses.
  We first show that inexact GD on top of standard robust aggregation procedures obtains optimal asymptotic error in the Byzantine setting. Going further, we study an algorithm for Optimization under Similarity, in which the server leverages an auxiliary loss function that approximates the global loss. Then, we introduce an Accelerated Extra-gradient method that yields acceleration in both the standard and similarity settings. We first give new general convergence results for these inexact schemes, improving the tolerance level of acceleration to a relative error term by a $κ^{1/2}$ factor over previous analysis, and then instantiate these results in the Byzantine setting through our reduction. Both algorithms drastically reduce the communication complexity, as we show theoretically and empirically.

Optimization and Control.title: Convergence of potential-preserving annealed Sinkhorn algorithm
Optimization and Control.summary: The annealed Sinkhorn algorithm is an iterative method for approximating solutions of optimal transport problems, in which the entropic regularisation parameter is progressively decreased. As this parameter decreases, one may preserve either the multiplicative scaling factors or the corresponding dual potentials. We study the potential-preserving iterates under positive, non-increasing regularisation schedules tending to zero. We prove that, if the schedule is non-summable, the iterates admit a subsequence converging to a solution of the corresponding optimal transport problem. The non-summability condition is sharp, as for every summable schedule in this class we construct an example in which the iterates converge to a plan violating the prescribed source marginal. We further establish convergence of the entire sequence if the relative inverse-temperature increments are also square-summable, and show by example that non-summability alone does not guarantee full convergence. Our convergence conditions are satisfied by linear inverse-temperature schedules, under which recent work has shown that the scaling-preserving iterates fail to converge to a solution of the optimal transport problem. We also derive convergence rates for polynomial inverse-temperature schedules up to and including linear growth, extending the marginal KL bound obtained by mirror-descent analysis at fixed temperature. Our best rate for the transport cost gap after rounding improves on that established for scaling-preserving annealing. Simple numerical illustrations accompany these convergence results.
Optimization and Control.comment: 26 pages, 2 figures. A short (early-stage) version of this paper was accepted for presentation at the Geometric Distributional Deep Learning Workshop at NeurIPS 2026

Optimization and Control.title: A Computational Study for Solving Decision-Dependent Robust Problems as Bilevel Optimization Problems
Optimization and Control.summary: Both bilevel and robust optimization are established fields of mathematical optimization and operations research. However, only until recently, the similarities in their mathematical structure has neither been studied theoretically nor exploited computationally. Based on the recent results by Goerigk et al. (2025), this paper is the first one that provides an extensive computational study for solving strictly robust optimization problems with decision-dependent uncertainty sets as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. If the uncertainty set can be dualized, the respective bilevel techniques to obtain a single-level reformulation are very similar compared with the classic dualization techniques used in robust optimization but lead to larger single-level problems to be solved. Our numerical study shows that this usually leads to larger computation times. For the more challenging case of decision-dependent uncertainty sets represented by mixed-integer linear models, one cannot apply classic dualization techniques from robust optimization. Thus, we compare the presented bilevel approach with an established method from the literature, which is based on quantified mixed-integer linear programs. Our numerical results indicate that, for the problem class of decision-dependent robust optimization problems with mixed-integer linear uncertainty sets, the bilevel approach performs better in terms of computation times.

Optimization and Control.title: Kantorovich Distance via Spanning Trees: Properties and Algorithms
Optimization and Control.summary: We study optimal transport between probability measures supported on the same finite metric space, where the ground cost is a distance induced by a weighted connected graph. Building on recent work showing that the resulting Kantorovich distance can be expressed as a minimization problem over the set of spanning trees of this underlying graph, we investigate the implications of this reformulation on the construction of an optimal transport plan and a dual potential based on the solution of such an optimization problem. In this setting, we derive an explicit formula for the Kantorovich potential in terms of the imbalanced cumulative mass (a generalization of the cumulative distribution in R) along an optimal spanning tree solving such a minimization problem, under a weak non-degeneracy condition on the pair of measures that guarantees the uniqueness of a dual potential. Our second contribution establishes the existence of an optimal transport plan that can be computed efficiently by a dynamic programming procedure once an optimal spanning tree is known. Finally, we propose a stochastic algorithm based on simulated annealing on the space of spanning trees to compute such an optimal spanning tree. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed approach for optimal transport on finite metric spaces.

Optimization and Control.title: When majority rules, minority loses: bias amplification of gradient descent
Optimization and Control.summary: Despite growing empirical evidence of bias amplification in machine learning, its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. We develop a formal framework for majority-minority learning tasks, showing how standard training can favor majority groups and produce stereotypical predictors that neglect minority-specific features. Assuming population and variance imbalance, our analysis reveals three key findings: (i) the close proximity between ``full-data'' and stereotypical predictors, (ii) the dominance of a region where training the entire model tends to merely learn the majority traits, and (iii) a lower bound on the additional training required. Our results are illustrated through experiments in deep learning for tabular and image classification tasks.

Optimization and Control.title: On convergence rate bounds for Markovian push-sum algorithms
Optimization and Control.summary: In this work we establish an upper bound on the almost sure convergence rate of a broad class of push-sum algorithms, more precisely for those where message passing events follow a Markovian dynamics, or a Hidden Markov Model.
