In this context, having a computationally accessible quantity at hand is of top priority; we thus formulate tools to cut down the complexity of obtaining the stated bound. Furthermore, we introduce a transformation to adjust a given push-sum scheme in a way that the bound on the rate provably improves -- and often so does the true convergence rate. Theoretical understanding is complemented by numerical results, where the quality of all three directions is demonstrated: for the bound on the rate, for the computational complexity and for the improvement strategy.

Optimization and Control.title: Nearly-Tight Oracle Complexity of Packing and Covering Linear Programs
Optimization and Control.summary: We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. Our algorithm breaks the $1/ε^2$ barrier of width-independent, $(1+ε)$-multiplicative error parallel solvers from prior work, improving the scaling with the error $ε>0$ to $1/ε,$ with total number of arithmetic operations scaling near-linearly with $1/ε$ and the number of nonzero entries of the constraint matrix.

Optimization and Control.title: Random Feature Neural Networks for Stochastic Optimal Control
Optimization and Control.summary: Random feature neural networks (RFNNs) sample their hidden parameters once and train only the output layer. We analyze RFNNs as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives. A policy change alters later states, so the error that matters is the objective error of the induced trajectory rather than a pointwise regression error. We extend the quantitative random-feature approximation theory for PDE solutions and nonlinear regression to feedback control. We investigate the objective error of an RFNN policy through two sources, approximation of the policy by random features and estimation of the objective from finitely many paths. A stability estimate for the controlled trajectory turns a policy error into an objective error. Under bounded actions, a regular benchmark policy and exact empirical minimization, the expected objective gap to the benchmark policy is at most of order $N^{-1/2}+\sqrt{N(1+\log N)/n}$, with $N$ the feature width per output coordinate and $n$ the number of paths. At fixed sample size the two terms trade off in $N$, and balancing them gives $N\asymp\sqrt{n/\log n}$. Across a wide range of examples, estimated gaps generally decrease with width and sample size, and RFNNs show an advantage when simulated paths are limited. We also study Parsimonious Random Feature Learning (PRFL), which grows and prunes the random dictionary during training while training only the output coefficients. At matched retained width and training budget, PRFL improves on a fixed RFNN in the LQ and Heston comparisons, while the fully trained network remains best in those examples.

Optimization and Control.title: Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors
Optimization and Control.summary: Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. This paper analyzes which closed-loop guarantees remain under these limitations for continuous-time nonlinear systems. We consider a value iteration scheme in which each iteration solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem with the previous iterate as terminal cost, and the associated controller applies the optimal input of this problem over each horizon in a sampled-data fashion. We show that if the convergence tolerance and the approximation error are small enough, the controller asymptotically stabilizes the system on sublevel sets of the computed iterate, and provide a suboptimality bound. This condition consists of pointwise inequalities that can be checked for the computed iterate, without establishing convergence of the iteration, and is a first step towards sample-based certification. We further establish inherent robustness of the controller with respect to model errors and recover classical results for the linear-quadratic regulator. Numerical studies on a linear-quadratic problem and on a nonlinear system with known optimal value function are consistent with the guarantees and show that the suboptimality bound is conservative.

Optimization and Control.title: A Matrix Lee-Sidford Barrier and Faster Semidefinite Programming
Optimization and Control.summary: We construct a matrix analog of the Lee-Sidford barrier for semidefinite programming (SDP) with $m$ equality constraints and $n$-by-$n$ matrices. The barrier has self-concordance parameter $\widetilde{O}(m)$, so short-step interior-point methods require only $\widetilde O(\sqrt m)$ iterations. We also show that our matrix Lee-Sidford barrier can be implemented efficiently by developing a randomized algorithm that solves SDPs with $m\leq n$ to accuracy $ε$ in $(n^{ω+o(1)}+n^2m^{3/2+o(1)})\operatorname{polylog}(1/ε)$ time, where $ω\leq 9/4$ is the matrix multiplication exponent, achieving the fastest known running time in this regime.

Optimization and Control.title: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $β$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $β$.
Optimization and Control.comment: 17 pages, 1 figure. Changes include the title, formulation of Conjecture 1 and Theorem 1(b) and proof of Theorem 1

Optimization and Control.title: Via a New LP Relaxation: Stronger Performance Guarantees for WSEPT, and an LP-Based Proof of Kawaguchi & Kyan
Optimization and Control.summary: We present a new linear programming relaxation for minimizing the total weighted completion time on identical parallel machines. Its right-hand side is supermodular, so the relaxation can be solved by a greedy algorithm. We show that the WSPT rule is within a factor $\frac{1}{2}(1 + \sqrt{2})$ of the optimal LP value. This bounds the integrality gap of the relaxation and gives a short, LP-based proof of the tight bound of Kawaguchi and Kyan on the performance of WSPT. We then turn to the stochastic version of the problem, in which processing times are independent random variables whose squared coefficients of variation are at most~$Δ$. A variance-corrected version of the new LP relaxation is valid for all non-anticipatory policies, and we show that WSEPT is within a factor $1 + (1 + Δ)/(3 + \sqrt{7 + 2 Δ})$ of it for $Δ\ge 1$, for any number of machines. This is $O(\sqrtΔ)$, whereas all previous guarantees for this problem grow linearly in $Δ$. Up to a constant factor, our bound matches the known $Ω(\sqrtΔ)$ lower bound for WSEPT. For $Δ\le 1$, we recover the best known bounds.

Optimization and Control.title: Learning and Dynamic Route Recommendation Under Unknown Traveler Compliance and Road Conditions
Optimization and Control.summary: Route planning during evacuations and other large-scale egress operations is inherently dynamic: the planner's recommendations affect future congestion on the roads, influence whether travelers accept their guidance, and determine what the planner can learn from the travelers' actual route choices. In this paper, we consider stochastic dynamic route recommendation to many travelers over a finite horizon under uncertain compliance and road conditions. In each period, a planner assigns routes that lead different origins' traveler groups to safe destinations, and travelers either follow the recommendation or revert to a preferred route. We model compliance using a logistic model and learn its unknown coefficients from observed route travel. We also filter the state of road conditions from noisy telemetry, and use a performance state to capture how the quality of past route recommendation affects travelers' future compliance. To determine the route assignment policy, we formulate a finite-horizon, belief-state dynamic program, show that the information state is sufficient for optimal Markov control, and develop an approximation that combines compliance beliefs with proximal policy optimization (PPO) using a Dirichlet actor over feasible route shares. We conduct numerical studies on instances of Eastern Massachusetts highway network data under different uncertain road conditions and compliance behavior. We demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of the PPO method and the value of dynamic adaptive solutions, against static routes. Our solutions reduce the mean and upper-tail costs of all travelers relative to myopic policy benchmarks, even when these benchmarks know the true compliance coefficients. Moreover, updating beliefs and the performance state dynamically also reduces the total cost under accurate, biased, and diffuse priors.

Optimization and Control.title: Contextual Distributionally Robust Optimization with Causal and Continuous Structure
Optimization and Control.summary: WWe propose a framework for contextual distributionally robust optimization (DRO) that considers the causal and continuous structure of the underlying distribution, and we develop interpretable and tractable decision rules. We first introduce the causal Sinkhorn discrepancy (CSD), an entropy-regularized causal Wasserstein distance that encourages continuous transport plans while preserving causal consistency. We then formulate a contextual DRO model with a CSD-based ambiguity set, termed Causal Sinkhorn DRO (Causal-SDRO), and derive its strong dual reformulation, where the worst-case distribution is characterized as a mixture of Gibbs distributions. To obtain an (infinite-dimensional) optimal policy, we propose a soft regression forest (SRF) decision rule: it preserves the interpretability of classical decision trees while being fully parametric, differentiable, and Lipschitz-smooth, enabling intrinsic interpretation from both global and local perspectives. To solve Causal-SDRO with parametric decision rules, we develop an efficient stochastic compositional gradient algorithm that converges to an $\varepsilon$-stationary point with $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ iteration complexity and $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-5})$ sample complexity. Finally, numerical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superior performance and interpretability of our method.

Optimization and Control.title: Smart predict-then-robustly-optimize
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we propose and study a robust variant of the smart predict-then-optimize approach that accounts for prediction shifts due to disturbance in the covariate feature space. While traditional integrated-learning-and-optimization models assume that side information is perfectly revealed, empirical data-driven features are frequently corrupted or noisy at the time of decision-making, leading to fragile operational policies. To bridge this gap, we integrate principles of robust optimization directly into the predictive-prescriptive pipeline via a smart predict-then-robustly optimize loss and establish a computationally tractable convex surrogate, designed to hedge against worst-case feature perturbations. On the theoretical front, we formalize the structural validity of this surrogate by proving its approximation error probability decays exponentially according to a sub-Gaussian concentration profile. Furthermore, we establish that under mild assumptions, the surrogate is Fisher consistent with high probability. We also prove necessary conditions under which our framework outperforms standard smart predict-then-optimize and maintain its superiority even when the standard method is equipped with regularized upstream predictions. Numerical experiments validate that our robust framework consistently yields significant performance improvements over standard methods, both in out-of-sample terms and in training stability.
Optimization and Control.comment: There is a mathematical flaw in the current version. We are working to correct it and produce a mathematically sound version of the paper

Optimization and Control.title: Differential inclusions and the chattering phenomenon
Optimization and Control.summary: This is a second draft of a manuscript about existence of solutions of differential inclusions involving chattering.

Optimization and Control.title: A structured quasi-Newton augmented Lagrangian algorithm for nonlinear least squares with linear and nonlinear constraints
Optimization and Control.summary: We present an algorithm for solving nonlinear least-squares problems subject to a mix of nonlinear constraints, linear equalities, and bounds. The nonlinear constraints are handled through an augmented Lagrangian reformulation of the objective, while the linear constraints are kept explicit. Each outer iteration therefore requires the approximate minimization of the augmented Lagrangian over a polyhedron, which we carry out with a gradient projection technique combined with a trust-region step computation. To capture the second-order information specific to the least-squares structure, we approximate the Hessian of the augmented Lagrangian by a Gauss--Newton term corrected by a structured quasi-Newton update, activated by a hybrid switching rule. The correction is built from a secant equation that we derive for the augmented Lagrangian itself. The outer iteration follows the augmented Lagrangian framework of Conn, Gould, Sartenaer and Toint for linearly constrained subproblems, for which we provide an explicit inner solver: a trust-region method whose Cauchy point is computed along nested faces of the polyhedron, without any projection onto it, and safeguarded by classical active-set devices, namely the release of bounds based on least-squares multiplier estimates and $\varepsilon$-active bounds. We prove that this inner solver satisfies the stopping rule required by the outer analysis, which yields global convergence of the overall method to a first-order critical point, and report numerical experiments. Our method outperforms an augmented Lagrangian solver built on the same outer update rules but without least-squares structure, and is competitive in computation time with a state-of-the-art solver for nonlinear programming.

Optimization and Control.title: Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels
Optimization and Control.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. To dynamically adjust the spatial resolution of the surrogate model, this approach utilizes a recursive splitting criterion. Furthermore, we develop a sampling allocation theory, establishing that driving the regional acquisition suprema below a common target level is achieved by polynomially denser sampling in rougher subdomains. Numerical experiments across homogeneous functions, synthetic inhomogeneous functions, and a real-world 8-dimensional LASSO hyperparameter tuning task demonstrate that our approach improves optimization efficiency on synthetic inhomogeneous functions, while performing comparably to Classic BO on homogeneous functions and on the LASSO task. This demonstrates the robustness of the adaptive partitioning mechanism.

Optimization and Control.title: Global Stability Analysis of an Excitable Infinite-Dimensional System
Optimization and Control.summary: Motivated by the study of excitable control of infinite-dimensional linear systems, we investigate the global stability properties of a closed-loop system consisting of a stable linear infinite-dimensional plant and a non-monotone controller. The controller has piecewise-linear dynamics that resemble the FitzHugh-Nagumo model of neural behaviour. As our main result, we derive a checkable condition for the global exponential stability of the closed-loop system using the circle criterion. Finally we illustrate the stability result for a one-dimensional heat equation.
Optimization and Control.comment: 7 pages, 8 figures, submitted to the European Control Conference 2027

Optimization and Control.title: Proper and Optimal Scoring Rules for Risk-Averse Agents
Optimization and Control.summary: Scoring rules are used to elicit probabilistic beliefs through payments that depend on reports and realised outcomes. We ask how these rules should be designed to induce truthful reporting and incentivise costly information acquisition when the agent is risk averse. For agents with entropic risk preferences in finite state spaces, we characterise proper scoring rules through an exponential transformation, derive optimal structures for information acquisition under bounded payments, and obtain explicit optimal coefficients in the binary case. The risk-neutral limit preserves properness and, in the binary case, optimality, while recovering the optimal betting structure for nonbinary states. For optimal design in the binary model, it suffices to focus on rules whose associated concave function is affine on each side of the prior. The optimal coefficients depend only on the prior and the risk-aversion parameter. The binary optimal rules we construct also admit an exact transformation from a particular risk-neutral optimal rule. In the nonbinary model, optimal design reduces to choosing the best prior bound in a transformed betting mechanism.

Optimization and Control.title: Fast Gradient-Based Framework for Spatial and Length Optimization of Geothermal Borehole Fields
Optimization and Control.summary: Common analytical design tools for Borehole Heat Exchanger (BHE) fields size the total drilling length for a given layout but do not optimize the positions of the boreholes. We introduce a framework (OptiGeoS) for the simultaneous, gradient-based optimization of the borehole length and the continuous borehole positions under groundwater advection. It couples the Moving Finite Line Source model with local BHE equations and evaluates the temporal convolutions by Fast Fourier Transforms. The gradients with respect to the length and the positions are computed analytically. A flow-dependent Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation confines each borehole to its own cell, which enforces the spatial separation and provides advection-informed layouts. Under purely conductive conditions, the fluid temperature extremes of the forward model for a single borehole lie between those of EED and GHEtool, which differ by $0.32\,\mathrm{K}$. For a field of 120 boreholes, the hourly outlet temperature agrees with that of EED with an RMSE of $0.28\,\mathrm{K}$, while the peak temperatures deviate by up to $2\,\mathrm{K}$. For 25 boreholes simulated hourly over 20 years, one forward simulation takes less than $0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ and a full optimization about $8\,\mathrm{min}$ on a laptop CPU. In a case study with groundwater advection, the optimized layout requires $16.2\,\%$ less borehole length than a fixed grid. It reduces the length increase caused by the advected thermal plume from $20.9\,\%$ to $1.4\,\%$.

Optimization and Control.title: Projector-Based Conic Formulations and Exact Decompositions for Distance-Based Assignment
Optimization and Control.summary: Given a set of fixed origin points and a set of variable target points in the same ambient metric space, we study distance-based assignment problems in which target placement and the assignment of origins to targets are determined simultaneously to minimize the overall distance-induced cost. We show that the assignment structure can be represented using orthogonal projection matrices. This observation leads to new mixed-projection conic formulations that avoid the big-$M$ envelopes used in standard mixed-integer models. Building on these formulations, we develop exact decomposition algorithms that separate the discrete selection of assignment projectors from the convex conic subproblems for target location. We also derive semidefinite relaxation bounds and primal procedures that provide warm starts for the exact methods. The proposed approach establishes new connections between distance-based assignment, orthogonal projectors, and low-rank semidefinite optimization, and applies to general conic-representable metrics.

Optimization and Control.title: A Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation for Automated Aircraft Arrival Routing and Scheduling
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the problem of computing dynamic arrival routes (DARs) in a terminal maneuvering area (TMA) together with an automated scheduling of all the arrivals within a given time interval. DARs are aircraft arrival routes from all entry points of a TMA, which merge traffic in that time interval towards the runway, and are modeled as energy-efficient continuous-descent operations, such that separation based on wake-turbulence categories is guaranteed within the TMA. We propose a new model based on a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation of a previous model for this problem. As in the previous model, we include tree consistency across consecutive planning intervals. However, the reformulation enables us to further improve the model and also consider aircraft that remain in the TMA from the previous period, a feature critical for operational safety. In computational experiments for Stockholm Arlanda airport, the new model consistently outperforms the previous one: we obtain solutions within 5 seconds to 12.65 minutes compared to up tp 40.9 hours with the old model for instances of half hours with high traffic. In addition, we are able to solve instances of a full hour of arriving aircraft with high traffic (33 aircraft) within 22.22 to 58.57 minutes, whereas the old model could not solve these instances at all. While we schedule all aircraft as continuous-descent arrivals, our model can be applied to any type of speed profiles for the arriving aircraft.

Optimization and Control.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
Optimization and Control.summary: Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. We introduce Low-Rank Multimarginal Optimal Transport (LRMOT), which restricts transport plans to tensors with bounded multilinear rank, providing a compact and structured representation of multimarginal couplings. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.

Optimization and Control.title: Distributed Constraint-coupled Resource Allocation: Anytime Feasibility and Violation Robustness
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper considers distributed resource allocation problems (DRAPs) with a coupled constraint for real-time systems. Based on primal-dual methods, we adopt a control perspective for optimization algorithm design by synthesizing a safe feedback controller using control barrier functions to enforce constraint satisfaction. On this basis, a distributed anytime-feasible resource allocation (DanyRA) algorithm is proposed. It is shown that the DanyRA algorithm converges to the exact optimal solution of DRAPs while preserving feasibility of the coupled inequality constraint from a feasible initialization. To address constraint violations caused by external disturbances, we develop a recover-after-violation mechanism using a virtual queue with a minimum buffer, enabling feasibility recovery within a prescribed number of iterations. We characterize the trade-off between convergence accuracy and violation robustness for a fixed positive buffer and establish exact convergence with a suitably decaying buffer. DanyRA is further specialized to coupled equality constraints, with constraint preservation and an explicit linear convergence rate established. Finally, a numerical example is provided for verification.

Optimization and Control.title: Inferring behind-the-meter demand components from net load via inverse optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Understanding and forecasting electricity demand responses to price signals is essential to support the operational decisions of system operators, retailers, and regulators. Traditional time series and machine learning approaches have performed well under stable consumption patterns. However, the rise of active consumers with flexible assets, such as solar-plus-storage systems and electric vehicles, introduces new complexities. These consumers exhibit behind-the-meter behavior that is generally unobservable to system operators and retailers, who can typically only measure net demand at the boundary meters which are located at the connection points to the grid. Net demand reflects the aggregate of baseload consumption, flexible load shifting, and self-generation, all of which may respond nonlinearly to market prices. As these unobservable components grow, existing forecasting models may fail to capture the true dynamics of consumer behavior. This work develops and implements a data-driven inverse optimization framework to reveal behind-the-meter consumption patterns using only net demand data. By analyzing net demand as revealed at the grid connection point, we estimate parameters for a latent optimization model, enabling predictions that infer the unobservable components. This enables more accurate point and probabilistic forecasting of electricity demand under varying price signals. Thus, it provides actionable insights for system operators to improve local congestion management and flexibility extraction, as well as for retailers and aggregators, who could thereby optimize operations and tariffs to leverage consumer flexibility. We validate the methodology using real-world data, demonstrating improved forecasting accuracy over leading machine learning and time-series benchmarks.

Optimization and Control.title: On the global convergence of gradient flow for wide shallow models beyond homogeneous nonlinearities
Optimization and Control.summary:
A surprising phenomenon in the training of neural networks is the ability of gradient descent to find global minimizers of the training loss despite its non-convexity. Following earlier work, we investigate this behavior for wide shallow models. Existing global convergence results primarily concern models with positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities, such as ReLU activations, and models with scalar output weights and bounded nonlinearities, such as sigmoid activations. We study a broader class of models, including multi-head attention layers and two-layer fully connected networks with bounded or asymptotically positively one-homogeneous activations and vector output weights.
  Building upon (Chizat and Bach, 2018), we prove that, in the limit of infinitely many hidden neurons or attention heads, non-minimizers of the training loss are unstable under the mean-field gradient flow dynamics by constructing "escape regions" in the parameter space. Our global convergence statements are conditional in the following sense: if the mean-field gradient flow converges for the Wasserstein 2-distance, then its limit must be a global minimizer. We revisit the bounded nonlinearity, scalar-output setting of (Chizat and Bach, 2018), giving an escape region construction adapted to unbounded nonlinear parameter domains. We also propose new constructions for nonlinearities with at most linear growth under a non-degeneracy assumption and for asymptotically positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities. Finally, we show the well-posedness and stability estimates for the mean-field training dynamics under sub-Gaussian initializations.

Optimization and Control.title: Linearization and local controllability of nonautonomous differential inclusions
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper we study the linearization of nonautonomous differential inclusions, whose right-hand side is integrably Lipschitz in the state variable and measurable in time. We establish measurability results for time-dependent graphs and identify the Clarke tangent cone to the set of their measurable selections in $L^\infty\times L^1$. Combining this characterization with a subtransversality argument, we obtain a lower estimate for the Clarke tangent cone to the set of all admissible trajectories starting from a fixed set. As an application, we give sufficient conditions for local controllability around a closed terminal set.

Optimization and Control.title: MASTO: Missed-thrust Aware Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. Therefore, in this work, we utilize a stochastic hybrid system framework to model a spacecraft as a Markov jump system that can switch between nominal and failure mode. We formulate the Missed-thrust resilient trajectory optimization problem as a Markov jump covariance steering problem, and propose a sequential convex programming-based approach, which can also respect chance constraints. We demonstrate our framework on two complex three-dimensional transfers in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three body problem, showcasing robustness against a range of MTEs, while respecting chance constraints. We further analyze controller performance across a range of MTE-probability distributions, offering valuable insights into the MTE-resilient trajectory design trade space.

Optimization and Control.title: Support monotonicity for quadratically regularized optimal transport
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the support of the optimizer $π_\varepsilon$ of the quadratically regularized optimal transport problem for quadratic cost and compactly supported marginals. As $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, this support converges to the support of the Monge coupling. We investigate whether the regularized supports are nested as $\varepsilon $ decreases. Under regularity assumptions on the marginal densities, their domains, and the Brenier map, we establish interior support inclusions in every dimension. More precisely, for each compact $K\subset\operatorname{int}X$ and fixed $θ\in(0,1)$, we prove that $\mathrm{spt}π_δ\cap(K\times Y) \subseteq\mathrm{spt}π_\varepsilon\cap(K\times Y)$ whenever $0<δ\leθ\varepsilon $ and $\varepsilon$ is sufficiently small. On these points, the rescaled density $\varepsilon dπ_\varepsilon/d(μ\otimesν)$ is bounded below by a positive multiple of $\varepsilon^{2/(d+2)}$. Our analysis combines sharp potential estimates with affine rescaling and a Liouville theorem that identifies the unique limiting density of the rescaled problem.

Optimization and Control.title: Remotest Operator Control String-Averaging Methods in Feasibility-Seeking
Optimization and Control.summary: The string-averaging (SA) method is a versatile algorithmic scheme for solving feasibility-seeking problems. It partitions the index set of all constraints into subsets of indices, called strings, allowing the user to apply operators successively along each string separately, and thus in parallel. The end-points of all such string operations are convexly combined to create the next iterate. Due to its flexible framework, SA is not restricted solely to this procedure; however, this characteristic applies only to the simultaneous step, while the sequential one is restricted to operator compositions. To permit alternative strategies in the latter, a novel algorithmic structure termed the Skeletal SA is introduced. Although its convergence is not established, it serves as a foundational "parent" structure that unveils unexamined SA algorithmic structures, as well as other known methods, obscured by standard compositions. To demonstrate the benefit of adopting the Skeletal SA framework over the standard SA scheme, we investigate a new approach, where instead of passing sequentially over each string via compositions, we employ a remotest-set-control-like strategy on every string by identifying the index of the operator farthest from the current iterate, and invoking it. This method favorably handles the common fixed point problem (CFPP), which requires finding a point within the intersection of finitely many constraint sets whose intersection is nonempty. Many iterative methods, including SA ones, have been proposed to solve the CFPP due to its importance in many scientific fields. However, remotest operator control SA (ROC-SA) methods have remained unexamined in this context.

Optimization and Control.title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does
Optimization and Control.summary: Different optimization algorithms can find very different solutions to the same problem. Gradient descent (GD) exhibits a low-rank bias in overparameterized problems when initialized near zero, while Adam does not. GD is rotationally equivariant: rotating both factors of a factored model $W = UV^\top$ by an orthogonal matrix leaves the loss unchanged, and GD's solution rotates accordingly. In contrast, Adam is not. We show that any algorithm using only the current gradient and respecting rotational symmetry amounts to a left-preconditioner depending only on the gradient's Gram matrix. This gives a norm-based test, which passes for the spectral norm in Muon and fails for Adam's $\ell_\infty$ norm. Empirically, nine optimizers fall into groups consistent with the test on underdetermined matrix sensing. Sharing Adam's second moment across coordinates gradually recovers a low-rank bias, and its solutions approach GD's as the stepsize decreases. On four hyperspectral scenes, Adam's solutions are hundreds to thousands of times further from GD's than two GD runs with different step sizes are from each other. In transformers and LoRA adapters, Adam separates two rotationally equivalent models from the first iteration, and learns higher-rank attention updates. Overall, recovering particular solutions depends on the optimizer's invisible coordinate basis, as well as how fast it grows small singular values relative to large ones.

Optimization and Control.title: Silver rate is sharp for gradient descent
Optimization and Control.summary: We determine the minimax convergence rate of gradient descent with predetermined real stepsizes on smooth convex functions up to an absolute constant factor. Let $p=\log_2(1+\sqrt{2})\approx 1.2716$. We prove that for every $L>0$, every integer $n\ge1$ and every stepsize schedule $h\in\mathbb{R}^n$ there exist a convex $L$-smooth function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ in some finite dimension $d$, a minimizer $x_\star$ of $f$ and an initial point $x_0\neq x_\star$ such that the iterate $x_n$ of gradient descent with stepsizes $h$ satisfies $(f(x_n)-f(x_\star))/(L\|x_0-x_\star\|^2)\ge c\,n^{-p}$ with an absolute constant $c>0$. This lower bound matches the $O(n^{-p})$ upper bounds achieved by silver-type stepsize schedules and establishes the optimality of the silver rate up to an absolute constant factor. Previous lower bounds reached the optimal polynomial exponent for both nonnegative and signed schedules but retained subpolynomial losses. We remove these losses for all predetermined real stepsize schedules. The proof combines a quantitative stability estimate for a splitting inequality at the silver proportions with Moreau-envelope constructions that join prescribed gradient descent trajectories and with multiscale averaging over stepsize thresholds.

Optimization and Control.title: Characterization of stability radii for robustly asymptotically stable dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study linear time-invariant dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems.
  We characterize when the systems are robustly asymptotically stable and derive exact conditions and bounds when this property is lost under structure-preserving perturbations.

Optimization and Control.title: The response field approach to path integral control
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper investigates non-linear path integral control problems within the response field formalism of nonequilibrium field theory. The aim of this work is exploratory, based on the identification of correspondences between backward adjoint processes and the response field of non-equilibrium statistical physics, whose properties have not been set out in an optimal control setting. The response field is found to play an analogous role to the backward adjoint process under the stochastic maximum principle. In particular, the gradient of the optimal cost-to-go at the initial time, which is proportional to the optimal control, is given by the average of the response field at the initial time. In contrast to the case of non-equilibrium dynamics, the response function is found to be acausal in the control setting. The linear-quadratic case of path integral control is studied, confirming it as the free theory, meaning that solving the control problem is equivalent to completing the square and determining the propagator for a two point boundary value problem. The developments presented here are a necessary prelude to applications based on field theoretic approximation, for both path integral control and their dual inference problems.

Optimization and Control.title: First-Order Information from Noisy Comparison Oracles
Optimization and Control.summary: We study stochastic and deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization problems where neither the functions nor their derivatives can be computed or estimated and the only information about the objective is available via pairwise comparisons. We focus on a specific model of smooth comparison oracles, as in the Bradley-Terry and Thurstone models, in which the probability of a correct comparison depends smoothly on the function-value gap. We investigate what first-order information can be obtained from such comparisons in deterministic and stochastic settings, and how many comparisons are needed to estimate it. We show that the first-order information that such comparisons provide is a fixed positive multiple of the gradient of the objective. We propose a random-direction estimator of the comparison gradient and analyze its bias and variance. It reaches mean-squared error $\varepsilon^2$ with $O(d^2\varepsilon^{-4})$ comparisons when the sample functions have Lipschitz gradients, and $O(d^2\varepsilon^{-3})$ when their Hessians are also Lipschitz. We prove lower bounds of the same order in $d$ and $\varepsilon$ for all comparison-based estimators, so these numbers are necessary and our estimator is optimal in $d$ and $\varepsilon$. As an application, we use it in a stochastic gradient method to find a point that is approximately stationary with respect to comparisons. We also extend the estimator to nonsmooth objectives, for which it estimates a smoothed comparison gradient.

Optimization and Control.title: Rare Event Analysis via Stochastic Optimal Control
Optimization and Control.summary: Rare events, from biomolecular conformational changes and phase transitions to chemical reactions, are central to many physical systems, yet extremely difficult to study computationally because unbiased simulations seldom produce them. Transition Path Theory provides a rigorous statistical framework for analyzing such events: it characterizes the ensemble of reactive trajectories between two metastable states (reactant and product), and its central object, the committor function (the probability that the system next reaches the product rather than the reactant), encodes essential kinetic and thermodynamic information. We introduce a framework for committor estimation that builds on stochastic optimal control, with a principled formulation that grounds committor learning on capped hitting-time trajectories. In this framework the committor defines a feedback control, proportional to the gradient of its logarithm, that steers trajectories toward the reactive region, enabling sampling of reactive paths. As practical algorithms, we develop two training losses: a heuristic on-policy direct backpropagation loss and a principled off-policy Value Matching loss, for which we establish first-order optimality guarantees. Being off-policy, Value Matching can leverage simulated trajectories from alternative sampling processes and reuse them from a replay buffer, which enables efficient learning. In particular, we derive a reactive current-preserving sampling process that can accelerate exploration. On reversible and non-reversible dynamics, the framework yields more accurate committor estimates, reaction rates, and transition path samples than existing methods.

Optimization and Control.title: The Optimal D.C. Bound Is Dominated by the Reciprocal of the Lovász Theta Number
Optimization and Control.summary: We resolve a question left open by Anstreicher and Burer (J. Global Optim. 33, 299--312, 2005). For the standard quadratic formulation of the stability number, we prove that the optimal difference-of-convex (D.C.) bound is at most the reciprocal of the Lovász theta number. The dominance is strict whenever the Lovász theta number is not exact.

Optimization and Control.title: One-sided certification of surrogate near-minimizers: exact worst-case envelopes under strong convexity and smoothness
Optimization and Control.summary: We study target suboptimality for points that approximately minimize a surrogate objective. Unlike standard uniform perturbation estimates, the available comparison is one-sided, thresholded at a certified lower target level, and restricted to the entire surrogate-selected sublevel set. We first show that selected comparison alone cannot yield a finite worst-case guarantee, even for strongly convex quadratics with identical Hessians. A single scalar upper bound on the surrogate minimum closes this information gap and leads to a sharp general estimate. For pairs of $μ$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth objectives, we then solve the associated worst-case information problem exactly. We obtain a sharp feasibility barrier and a dimension-free envelope; in its nontrivial regime, the value reduces to a scalar maximization over a compact interval. Explicit one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic objectives attain the bound while satisfying the one-sided constraint on the full selected set. We characterize when curvature strictly improves the general certificate and provide a threshold-preserving finite-net validation procedure. The results identify the best guarantee permitted by the prescribed partial information, independently of any particular optimization algorithm or additive perturbation model.

Optimization and Control.title: A Trust-Region Interior-Point Stochastic Sequential Quadratic Programming Method
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we propose a trust-region interior-point stochastic sequential quadratic programming (TR-IP-SSQP) method for solving optimization problems with a stochastic objective and deterministic nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. In this setting, exact evaluations of the objective function and its gradient are unavailable, but their stochastic estimates can be constructed. In particular, at each iteration our method builds stochastic oracles whose estimates of the objective value and gradient satisfy proper adaptive accuracy conditions with a fixed probability. To handle inequality constraints, we adopt an interior-point method (IPM), in which the barrier parameter is taken from a prescribed decreasing sequence and is reduced once a stochastic stationarity test is passed. Under standard assumptions, we show that, almost surely, the KKT residual vanishes along the iterations at which the barrier parameter is reduced, and every limit point of these iterates is a KKT point. We implement the method on a subset of problems from the CUTEst test set, as well as on constrained logistic regression problems, to demonstrate its practical performance.

Optimization and Control.title: Communication-Efficient Decentralized Stochastic Minimax Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study decentralized stochastic nonconvex Polyak--Łojasiewicz minimax problems. Motivated by local SGD in federated learning, we improve communication efficiency by allowing agents to perform several local updates before the communication stage. Existing work gives a communication bound of $\mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{κ^3\varepsilon^{-2}}{(1-λ)^2}\Big)$ for local decentralized gradient descent--ascent using $\mathcal{O}\Big(\varepsilon^{-2}+\frac{κ^2\varepsilon^{-2}}{K(1-λ)}\Big)$ local updates per round. Here $\varepsilon$ is the target accuracy, $1-λ$ is the spectral gap and $κ\ge1$ is the condition number. However, too many local updates can leave available communication resources underused and increase local drift, as agents follow their own objectives for longer before exchanging information. We therefore pursue improved communication efficiency while keeping the number of local steps small. To this end, we propose DiMA, a structured local--global learning strategy that uses local updates to build an accelerated momentum and perform decentralized learning through either standard gossip or accelerated mixing. By exploiting the positive semidefiniteness of the mixing matrix, we derive complexity bounds for DiMA under different updating strategies. Experiments on robust logistic regression demonstrate improved performance over several existing baselines.

Optimization and Control.title: Supply Chain Networks: Equilibrium, Sensitivity, Dynamics and Shortage Games
Optimization and Control.summary: We model production in a supply chain network in which every node sets a Newsvendor order target, upstream demand is the sum of downstream orders routed through a substochastic matrix, and every node has a capacity. The clearing vector of production quantities is the unique Nash equilibrium of the ordering game and the unique optimal solution of a linear program, and it has the form of the Eisenberg--Noe interbank clearing model. Nodes that produce their order target are hedged; the others are unhedged. We give comparative statics and a closed form for the stationary covariance of node demands. Inventory drawdown after a capacity shock is a Skorokhod reflection problem with a closed-form solution: the network and the unhedged nodes determine who is eventually rationed and by how much, and inventories determine when. When rationed nodes can inflate their orders, the equilibria never lower aggregate deliveries and can make suppliers with no physical shortage unhedged. With endogenous prices, a per-epoch price equilibrium exists and, under mild conditions, is unique when supply is price-elastic. We illustrate the model on global crude-oil trade.

Optimization and Control.title: When Simpler Beats Learned: Dual-Weighted Sampling vs. Machine Learning for the Pricing Subproblem in Graph Coloring
Optimization and Control.summary: The graph coloring problem can be solved to optimality by branch-and-price (B&P), but its performance hinges on the column generation (CG) step, where each iteration requires solving a maximum weight independent set (MWIS) pricing problem. The state-of-the-art machine-learning (ML) pricing heuristic follows a prediction-sampling paradigm: a learned model scores each vertex of a graph, and independent sets are sampled from the induced distribution. We observe, however, that the scoring procedure does not need to be learned, and critically assess the role of ML by replacing the learned scores with the dual solution of the restricted master problem, resulting in Dual-Weighted Sampling, a proposed lightweight alternative that requires no feature engineering or training. Within a unified CG and B&P framework that varies only the pricing oracle, Dual-Weighted Sampling outperforms MLPH, hand-crafted heuristics, and exact solvers on the established graph coloring benchmark in both runtime and solution quality. In particular, it remains competitive on the DIMACS random family, where MLPH was shown strongest in the original evaluation, while achieving more than a two-fold speedup in CG runtime on recursive-sparse and real-world graph families.

Optimization and Control.title: From Distributional to Temporal Interactions in McKean--Vlasov Games and Control
Optimization and Control.summary: The paper examines the relation between time and population in stochastic games and control. The idea is to substitute the interaction described via the population law with the interaction described via the occupation measure of a single self-interacting trajectory. Thus we study how McKean--Vlasov fixed point games and Mean Field Control problems compare with their resulting self-interacting counterparts. Assuming appropriate dissipativity and regularity conditions, we find that the ergodic costs, value functions and optimal feedback sets are identical, and the fixed point equilibria are equivalent. In addition, we obtain uniform bounds on both trajectories and costs for finite horizon problems. These bounds allow proving asymptotic equivalence of the normalized value functions, and enable the transfer of equilibrium strategies and optimal feedbacks from one representation to another, with approximation errors that vanish as the horizon length increases.

Optimization and Control.title: Degenerate Preconditioned Proximal Point Algorithms as Forward Methods for Nonmonotone Inclusions
Optimization and Control.summary: We study degenerate preconditioned proximal point algorithms (PPPA) for finding zeros of nonmonotone set-valued operators in Hilbert spaces under solution-relative $(U,V)$-semimonotonicity, with possibly indefinite $U$ and $V$. With a closed-range preconditioner $P$, the reduced PPPA dynamics admit a forward representation through the complementary resolvent of a parallel composition, without requiring monotonicity or admissibility. Relative semimonotonicity of the range-restricted operator transfers to the reduced forward map, allowing our forward theory for possibly set-valued mappings to yield Fejér estimates and residual rates. Under suitable conditions, including demiclosedness of the reduced map at zero, the projected PPPA iterates and shadows converge weakly to a common projected zero. Without demiclosedness, a counterexample shows that the projected sequences may converge to a point outside the projected zero set, even when the original operator is continuous. Bounded recovery condition yields weak convergence of the full (non-projected) shadows. The monotonicity modulus $U$ yields additional results: under suitable conditions, $U\succeqτP$ with $τ>0$ gives strong and linear convergence of the projected PPPA sequences, while $U\succeq-σP$ with $0\leσ<1/2$ still permits local linear rates under metric subregularity. These strong convergence and linear rate guarantees extend to the full shadows when a Lipschitz recovery estimate holds, such as when $U$ is strongly monotone on $\ker P$. For Chambolle--Pock and Douglas--Rachford splitting, we establish Lipschitz recovery even when $U=0$ by exploiting the primal--dual structure. Under suitable parameter conditions, full-shadow convergence guarantees, including $R$-linear rates, extend to the original PPPA iterates.

Optimization and Control.title: Two energy methods for distributed port-Hamiltonian systems and their application to stability analysis
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop two local energy methods for distributed parameter port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems on one-dimensional spatial domains. The methods are applied to derive a characterization of exponential stability directly in terms of the energy passing through the boundary over a given time horizon. The resulting condition is verified for a network of vibrating strings where existing sufficient conditions cannot be applied. Moreover, we use a local energy method to study the short-time behavior of pH systems with boundary damping which was recently studied in the context of hypocoercivity.

Optimization and Control.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
Optimization and Control.summary: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

Optimization and Control.title: Continuous-Time LQR from a Single Discrete-Time Off-Policy Batch
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study discounted continuous-time linear--quadratic regulation (LQR) with unknown drift parameters and additive noise, using a single batch of discrete-time off-policy transitions. Discrete-time methods target a policy tied to the training interval, while shortening this interval can make learning from finite data more sensitive to noise. Learning an accurate continuous-time controller therefore requires balancing discretization and finite-sample errors while preserving stability throughout policy improvement. We develop a drift-only policy iteration algorithm, termed PhiBE-PI, using one quadratic state--action critic for policy evaluation and explicit greedy improvement. Reusing the batch makes later policies depend on the data. Exploiting the quadratic structure of LQR, we show that the data enter every policy evaluation only through one policy-independent empirical matrix, so a single high-probability bound controls all iterates.
  For sufficiently large discount~$β$, small observation intervals, and a sufficiently large batch, we prove that all iterates are stabilizing for the discounted problem and converge quadratically to a data-dependent fixed point. The gain bound separates iteration, finite-sample, and discretization errors. In this regime, the finite-sample and discretization terms scale as $1/(β\sqrt{nΔt})$ and $Δt/β$, respectively. The bounds thus reveal a tradeoff: at a fixed batch size, finer observations reduce discretization error but increase finite-sample error. Because PhiBE-PI approximates the continuous-time optimal gain rather than a discrete-time one, its policy can remain near-optimal when deployed at faster control rates. Experiments confirm this advantage over discrete-time Bellman-equation baselines when the observation interval is small relative to the system's time scale.

Optimization and Control.title: A Single-Loop, Constant-Batch First-Order Penalty Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Recent advances in penalty-based methods for stochastic bilevel optimization (SBO) have eliminated the need for second-order derivative oracles. However, for stochastic nonconvex-strongly convex bilevel problems, existing first-order methods typically rely on nested loops and/or large batch sizes for attaining $O(ε^{-6})$ or $O(ε^{-4})$ sample complexity under standard bounded-variance assumption or mean-square smoothness assumption. Achieving these rates with a single-loop penalty method and a constant batch size remains challenging due to a large penalty value needed for an accurate approximation. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic SIngle-loop COnstant-Batch first-order penalty method (SICO) that combines two complementary ingredients. First, it performs one stochastic-gradient update per-iteration for both the original lower-level and penalized problems, with a projection that controls the separation between their iterates. Second, it applies an exponential moving average to stabilize the upper-level gradient estimator. We show that this combination achieves $ O(ε^{-6}) $ sample complexity using only $O(1)$ stochastic-gradient samples per iteration under unbiased, bounded-variance stochastic gradients. Under the additional mean-square smoothness assumption on the lower-level stochastic gradients, the same algorithm improves the complexity to $O(ε^{-4})$ also with $O(1)$ batch size. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to match the best-known convergence rate for fully first-order SBO methods using a single loop and a constant batch size. This result addresses an open problem posed in the literature.

Optimization and Control.title: Scaled Relative Graph Separation for Unbounded Nonlinear Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: We investigate stability analysis of one-channel nonlinear feedback systems based on the recent notion of scaled relative graph (SRG). Our focus is on the SRG separation in the complex plane for feedback stability analysis that involves possibly unbounded open-loop nonlinear systems. Subject to a technical assumption, a homotopy-based SRG separation theorem is developed as the main result, where the incremental directed gap is utilized as a key instrument to quantify robust feedback stability along the homotopy path. Doing so enables us to incorporate commonly used integrators as unbounded systems in the SRG-based framework. Specializations of the main result to linear systems, along with illustrative examples, are also provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.
Optimization and Control.comment: An extended version of a conference paper accepted for the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, 2026

Optimization and Control.title: Group Buying through Bankruptcy Rules: Cost Sharing and Endogenous Pricing
Optimization and Control.summary: Group buying allows independent buyers to pool their demand and benefit from quantity discounts that would not be available to them individually. While collective purchasing reduces total procurement costs, it raises a fundamental allocation question: how should the resulting savings be distributed among heterogeneous buyers? We address this question by integrating cost-allocation and bankruptcy approaches into a unified group-buying framework. Starting from a continuous quantity discount function, we examine cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and develop an endogenous pricing representation in which each buyer's effective discount may depend on the demand profile of the entire group. We then establish a connection between group buying and bankruptcy theory by interpreting the aggregate savings from cooperation as the estate and each buyer's potential savings as its claim. This formulation allows us to derive cost-allocation mechanisms based on the proportional, constrained equal awards, constrained equal losses, and Talmud rules. For each rule, we obtain the corresponding buyer-specific price function and characterize the associated variable discount factor. We further examine the relationships between bankruptcy-based and cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and use a numerical example with simulated data to compare their implications. The proposed framework links alternative fairness principles for allocating cooperative savings to economically interpretable pricing mechanisms, providing a unified basis for analyzing how group purchasing gains are distributed among heterogeneous buyers.

Optimization and Control.title: National-scale scheduling of long-distance electric vehicle charging under plug capacity
Optimization and Control.summary: Can today's U.S. public charging network serve long-distance trips by electric vehicles (EVs), and at what cost to travelers? We plan the charging stops of 2.2 million long-distance trips that need en-route charging, from a 1% sample of a one-month simulation, through the contiguous U.S. fast-charging network. Plans value detour, charging, and waiting time. Charging to a fixed battery level makes each trip's problem a shortest path, solved exactly; common modeling shortcuts can reverse the cost comparison. For trips competing for plugs, we compare four coordination methods, from none to reservations by departure time; the best two come within 2.2% and 6.1% of the best known solutions on small cases. First, if every plug serves every EV, existing fast chargers can reach 98.5% of the trips that need to charge, excluding those with an overly long link, with under four stops and about seven minutes of detour. Second, charging speed and electricity price decide the cost comparison: at \$0.15 per kWh, the EV is cheaper only for travelers valuing their charging time below \$11 per hour with 50 kW, or \$111 per hour with 350 kW chargers; at \$0.45 per kWh, it costs more at either speed. Third, without coordination, long queues form at several hundred small stations at 50 kW while nearby larger ones are less busy. If every trip books a plug, almost all waiting disappears on all trips at 350 kW for under a minute of extra detour, and at \$0.15 per kWh the EV trip stays about 21% cheaper.
Optimization and Control.comment: 35 pages, 3 figures, 12 tables; includes supplementary material

Optimization and Control.title: Small-time global exact controllability of nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with bilinear controls
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with nonlinearity $κ|ψ|^{2p}ψ$, a fixed smooth real potential $V$, and bilinear controls. Using only the three control potentials $\mathbf 1,\cos x,\sin x$, we prove global approximate controllability in $H^s$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$ for all integers $s,p\ge1$, every $κ\in\mathbb R$, and any prescribed positive time. The proof combines two ingredients: the approximate controllability between nowhere vanishing states from our companion paper, and a new mechanism that steers any nonzero initial state to a nowhere vanishing state in arbitrarily small time.
  When $V=0$ and the nonlinearity is defocusing or sufficiently weakly focusing, adding two explicit control potentials of finite regularity gives local exact controllability in $H^2$ near the constant state, via a moment problem and the inverse mapping theorem. Together, these results imply global exact controllability in $H^2$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$, at any prescribed positive time, with five control potentials. To~the best of our knowledge, this is the first global exact controllability result for a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with finitely many bilinear controls.

Optimization and Control.title: New Lower Bounds for Stochastic Non-Convex Optimization through Divergence Decomposition
Optimization and Control.summary: We study fundamental limits of first-order stochastic optimization in a range of nonconvex settings, including L-smooth functions satisfying Quasar-Convexity (QC), Quadratic Growth (QG), and Restricted Secant Inequalities (RSI). While the convergence properties of standard algorithms are well-understood in deterministic regimes, significantly fewer results address the stochastic case, where only unbiased and noisy gradients are available. We establish new lower bounds on the number of noisy gradient queries to minimize these classes of functions, also showing that they are tight (up to a logarithmic factor) in all the relevant quantities characterizing each class. Our approach reformulates the optimization task as a function identification problem, leveraging divergence decomposition arguments to construct a challenging subclass that leads to sharp lower bounds. Furthermore, we present a specialized algorithm in the one-dimensional setting that achieves faster rates, suggesting that certain dimensional thresholds are intrinsic to the complexity of non-convex stochastic optimization.
Optimization and Control.comment: Revised the examples arguments in the proof of Lemma 2.1. Corrected numerical constants, budget conditions, and terms involving the initial distance in the displayed SGD bounds. Clarified the role of auxiliary reference distributions in the lower-bound proofs. Refined concentration bounds and stopping arguments in the one-dimensional analysis. The main rates and algorithmic approach are unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Near-Optimal Smooth Convex Optimization with a Comparison Oracle
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the minimization of a convex $d$-dimensional function with $L$-Lipschitz gradient when the only available information is a comparison oracle that reports which of two points has the smaller objective value. Given an initial point within distance $R$ of a minimizer, the constants $L$ and $R$, and $A = LR^2/\varepsilon$, we give a deterministic method that returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal point using $O(\sqrt{A}\,[d\log(2dA)+\log^2(2A)])$ comparisons for $A\ge1$, counting all comparisons spent in inner subroutines. The method is based on a normalized variant of Nemirovski's subspace method: each iteration performs a line search along an estimated gradient direction followed by a minimization over a two-dimensional affine subspace, and both subroutines rely on a comparison oracle and basic arithmetic operations only. With exact function values, combining finite-difference gradients with an accelerated method gives the well-known bound of $O(d\sqrt{A})$ evaluations; our bound shows that one bit per query suffices to match it up to logarithmic factors. Since two function values determine one comparison, the exact function-value lower bound of Dorn et al. implies that our bound is optimal up to logarithmic factors when $32\le A\le d^2$.

Optimization and Control.title: A Single-Loop Method with Optimal Leading-Order Oracle Complexity for Optimization and Game Stationarity in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop a single-loop first-order framework for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, with matching leading-order upper and lower bounds for optimization and game stationarity in a projected zero-respecting oracle model. We propose a single-loop projected damped extragradient method coupling projected extragradient updates with dual momentum and a moving proximal center. Each iteration uses at most three gradient evaluations, without nested subproblems. For game stationarity, a deterministic best iterate has first-order residual below $\varepsilon$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}Δ_φ\varepsilon^{-5/2})$, where $L$ is the gradient Lipschitz constant, $D_Y$ bounds the dual feasible-set diameter, and $Δ_φ$ is the initial-point-dependent value-function gap. For optimization stationarity, a uniformly selected iterate has expected squared Moreau-envelope gradient norm at most $\varepsilon^2$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^2D_YΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-3})$. Matching lower bounds are $Ω(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}Δ_φ\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ for game stationarity and $Ω(L^2D_YΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-3})$ for optimization stationarity over projected zero-respecting first-order methods. Under dual strong concavity, the same framework achieves leading first-order oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtκLΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-2})$ under both criteria, where $κ$ is the dual condition number. Matching lower bounds hold for both criteria in the same oracle model. To our knowledge, this is the first work to close the oracle complexity gap for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization under both stationarity criteria by simultaneously improving upper and lower bounds in the projected zero-respecting oracle model.

Optimization and Control.title: Controlled nonstationary G-diffusions: dynamic programming, weighted Harris contraction and entrance risk
Optimization and Control.summary: We study controlled nonstationary \(G\)-diffusions in a canonical-law formulation of covariance uncertainty. The principal structural result is an abstract weighted Harris--oscillation contraction theorem for translation-covariant nonlinear evolution families. A Lyapunov estimate for a dominating terminal-perturbation bound and a local space--time oscillation estimate for differences imply exponential contraction in a weighted quotient norm, without positive homogeneity, subadditivity or convexity. For elementary sample-and-hold feedback controls and a rectangular family of martingale laws, we construct a measurable controlled state map and prove deterministic- and stopped-time dynamic programming principles for the robust lower value. Under uniform ellipticity, differences of Bellman values belong to a common parabolic Pucci class; a local Harnack argument and an all-policy Lyapunov estimate verify the abstract hypotheses. For zero running cost, the contraction yields a unique tempered entrance nonlinear expectation and exponential attraction. With running cost, it yields a unique normalized nonstationary corrector and an additive cocycle, together with exponential convergence of relative values. Subtracting a scalar primitive of the cocycle gives an all-time viscosity solution of the backward Bellman--Isaacs equation. Autonomous and periodic coefficients yield additive eigenpairs, stationary and periodic ergodic equations, and convergence of long-time average costs. The results provide a long-time theory for optimally controlled dynamic risk evaluation under nonstationary covariance uncertainty.

Optimization and Control.title: Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies
Optimization and Control.summary: Designing simple inventory policies becomes increasingly difficult as operational features and system configurations expand. We develop an Agentic Inventory-Policy Discovery System based on explicitly defined simple operational formula (SOF) policy and template classes. Large language models (LLMs) revise symbolic structures, while a numerical engine fits parameters separately for each instance and evaluates the induced policies. Multicriteria parent selection, state-specific operational diagnostics, and reusable symbolic motifs guide structural evolution. A three-stage progression develops shared templates across instances and configurations with varying state dimensions. Experiments on 15,600 instances spanning 50 demand distributions cover lead times, perishability, their combination, and lead times with limited customer patience. The discovered templates improve aggregate empirical performance over evaluated SOF benchmarks and are competitive with policies requiring more elaborate online computations. For a lost-sales system with a three-period lead time, we develop an average-cost decomposition and prove that, under specified demand and cost conditions, a capped dual-shortfall specialization of a discovered policy strictly outperforms every policy in the considered capped base-stock benchmark class. This analysis links the performance advantage to the discovered replenishment mechanism. Together, these results highlight the potential of agentic discovery to generate simple inventory policies with strong empirical performance and identify operational mechanisms amenable to rigorous theoretical analysis.

Optimization and Control.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
Optimization and Control.summary: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. Local cost inequalities reduce arbitrarily long switching cycles of a minimizer to six types. We exclude those types by geometric comparisons and rigorous finite verification, and identify the remaining short minimizer.
Optimization and Control.comment: 430 pages. The author hopes that further work will lead to a shorter and more beautiful proof

Optimization and Control.title: On Big-M Reformulations of Bilevel Linear Programs: Hardness of A Posteriori Verification
Optimization and Control.summary: A standard approach to solving optimistic bilevel linear programs (BLPs) is to replace the lower-level problem with its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions and reformulate the resulting complementarity constraints using auxiliary binary variables. This yields a single-level mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model involving big-$M$ parameters. While sufficiently large big-$M$s that preserve at least one bilevel-optimal solution can be computed in polynomial time, verifying a priori that given big-$M$s do not cut off any feasible or optimal lower-level solutions is known to be computationally difficult. In this paper, we establish two complementary hardness results. First, we show that, even with a single potentially incorrect big-$M$ parameter, it is coNP-complete to verify a posteriori whether a given optimal solution of the resulting MILP model is bilevel optimal. In particular, this negative result persists for min-max problems without coupling constraints and applies to strong-duality-based reformulations of mixed-integer BLPs. Second, we show that verifying global big-$M$ correctness remains computationally difficult a posteriori, even when an optimal solution of the MILP model is available.
Optimization and Control.comment: The proof of Theorem 3 has been substantially revised

Optimization and Control.title: Universal Extra-Gradient Method for Stochastic Variational Inequalities
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the stochastic Extra-Gradient Method (EGM) for solving a stochastic variational inequality (VI) over a compact convex set. The main assumption is $(δ, L)$-continuity of the VI mapping, which includes Hölder mappings and their linear combinations. We develop new adaptive, line-search-free step-size rules for stochastic EGM. These rules can be interpreted as enhanced AdaGrad-type updates and require no prior knowledge of either the continuity modulus of the VI mapping or the variance of the stochastic oracle. The resulting methods are universal and attain the best complexity bound among the admissible continuity regimes. We prove convergence guarantees in terms of an expected residual function that upper bounds the relevant accuracy measures for several important problem classes, including the dual gap for monotone VIs, and the primal-dual gap for saddle-point and optimization problems. For Hölder-continuous mappings, our bounds recover the optimal dimension-independent complexity of first-order methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Nonminimizing Attration of Stochastic Subgradient Methods on Semialgebraic Functions
Optimization and Control.summary: We construct a globally Lipschitz, coercive, semialgebraic function in two dimensions for which stochastic subgradient iterates converge to the origin, a Clarke critical point that is neither limiting critical nor a local minimizer. For power-law stepsizes, this attraction holds on open sets of initial points and linear tilts, uniformly over all noise sequences within a prescribed bound. The example shows that subdifferential regularity cannot be removed from the generic guarantee of convergence to local minimizers established by Davis, Drusvyatskiy, and Jiang (2026). For the same tilted objectives and initial points, the unique Clarke subgradient flow converges to a strict local minimizer. Thus, convergence of continuous-time flows to local minimizers cannot by itself justify the corresponding guarantee for discrete subgradient methods, even with diminishing stepsizes.
Optimization and Control.comment: 16 pages, 2 figures. This revision adds a proof that the Clarke subgradient flow converges to a strict local minimizer from the same open set of initial points for which the discrete iterates converge to the nonminimizing origin

Optimization and Control.title: Fully First-Order Optimization for Implicit Multilevel Compositions via Recursive Perturbations
Optimization and Control.summary: We study multilevel optimization problems in which the outer objective depends on a finite composition of implicit response maps defined by smooth inner functions. This model covers chains of strongly convex minimization responses, strongly convex--strongly concave saddle responses, or a mixture of the two. We propose a fully first-order method that estimates the outer gradient through recursive response perturbations. The main difficulty with approximate responses is that an adjoint error at one level changes the perturbation vector at the preceding level. To control this propagation, we pair the unperturbed and perturbed updates at each level and track their scaled differences jointly with the forward response errors. The resulting tracking bounds are uniform in the perturbation radius $δ$. For the exact composite objective, we establish an $O(K^{-1}+δ^2)$ bound on the average squared gradient norm after $K$ outer iterations. For fixed problem data and finite depth, a suitable choice of $δ$ yields $ε$-stationarity in $O(ε^{-2})$ outer iterations with inner budgets independent of the target accuracy. For strongly convex minimization chains, we also derive condition-number-dependent first-order oracle complexity bounds.

Optimization and Control.title: Sharp Volume Contraction of a Centrally Cut John Ellipsoid
Optimization and Control.summary:
