For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ in positive dimension, let $w(K)$ be the volume of its maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid. For a closed halfspace $H$ whose boundary passes through the center of that ellipsoid, we prove \[ w(K\cap H)\le R_nw(K),\qquad R_1=\frac12,\qquad R_n=\frac12\left(\frac n{n-1}\right)^{(n-1)/2}\quad(n\ge2), \] with equality attained in every fixed dimension. This refines the optimal dimension-independent bound from the author's earlier work on [Khachiyan's ellipsoid conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28447).
  We characterize the full equality family, including nonsimplex extremizers, and establish an exact volume-deficit identity that yields dimension-independent stability of the new ellipsoid and its weighted contact geometry in John coordinates. The proof reduces the problem to finite John contacts and constructs an explicit conic certificate by a transformation of contact directions and a common polar rotation. Its determinant is controlled by a nonnegative contact defect. The sharp contraction theorem, equality classification, stability estimates, and supporting results have been formally verified in Lean 4 using mathlib.

Optimization and Control.title: Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems
Optimization and Control.summary: We prove memory/query-complexity tradeoff lower bounds for the feasibility problem, where the goal is to find a point within an $ε$-ball hidden in the unit $d$-dimensional ball, with access to a separation oracle. This problem admits three regimes: the low-accuracy regime $ε\geq 1/\sqrt d$ where memory does not play a role, the medium-accuracy regime $1/\sqrt d\geq ε\geq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ where prior works identified strong memory/query-complexity separations, and the high-accuracy regime $ε\leq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ for which much less is known. In this regime, low-memory algorithms with significantly faster convergence rates than gradient descent have been developed in [BZJ24]: for accuracy $ε$ and any $δ\in[0,1]$, these require $d^{1+δ}\ln \frac1ε$ memory bits and use $\left(d\ln\frac1ε\right)^{O(d^{1-δ})}$ oracle queries. In comparison, gradient descent uses the same memory for $δ=0$ but requires $1/ε^2$ oracle queries. On the lower-bound side, no non-trivial memory/query-complexity tradeoff was known: the best lower bound remained the historical memory-independent bound $Ω(d\ln \frac1ε)$ from [NYD83]. We make progress towards characterizing the memory landscape in this high-accuracy regime by showing that for any $δ\in[0,1]$, any algorithm with $d^{1+δ}\ln\frac1ε$ bits of memory uses at least $\left(d\ln\frac1ε\right)^{\widetildeΩ(d^{(1-δ)/8})}$ oracle calls. This result justifies the seemingly peculiar exponential-in-$d$ dependence of oracle complexity for the aforementioned low-memory algorithms. In particular, our result shows that for high-accuracy feasibility problems, insufficient memory does result in an exponential price in the dimension for the query-complexity.
Optimization and Control.comment: Version note. This version revises the compression reduction and mutual-information accounting in Section 4.3. The revised argument explicitly includes the shared randomness in the Message between encoder and decoder

Optimization and Control.title: Learned spatial opportunity cost admission for ride-hailing with calibrated thresholds
Optimization and Control.summary: Ride-hailing operators must decide whether to accept a request before observing future demand. Serving a ride earns revenue and changes where and when the vehicle can serve again. We develop learned spatial opportunity cost admission for a centrally managed fleet. The policy estimates demand from past requests and solves a rolling mean-demand plan. Dual prices account for using a vehicle at its origin and returning it to service at its destination. With positive regularization, the policy accepts a request when its planned service fraction reaches a common threshold. We fix the regularization parameter and select the threshold using validation revenue. For one vehicle on a single route, we derive the exact range of thresholds that attain optimal expected revenue. When several origins share return demand at a hub, the best common threshold can lose revenue in proportion to fleet size. Independent validation bounds the revenue loss relative to the best candidate threshold. At a fixed threshold, under Poisson arrivals and a margin condition, the revenue gap between using estimated and true mean demand has a tight inverse-square-root bound in the number of historical days. We evaluate the policy on 60 synthetic instances across six demand families and on ten New York workdays across 25 taxi zones and three fleet sizes. With two validation days, calibration improves mean paired revenue over the default threshold by 4.93% in the synthetic study and 7.08% in New York. In New York, the policy earns 1.24% to 2.54% less than the best-performing benchmark in mean paired comparisons and takes about one-eleventh as long per decision. Calibration gains are largest for the smallest New York fleet. In the synthetic study, gains over accepting every feasible request are largest under commuting demand.

Optimization and Control.title: Critical Times for Local Controllability and Steady-State Transfer of a Water Tank
Optimization and Control.summary: We determine the critical times for a water tank governed by the one-dimensional Saint-Venant equations with horizontal acceleration as the control. Time is measured in units of the linear wave crossing time. For $C^1$ fluid trajectories and continuous controls, local exact controllability holds exactly for $T>T_c=2+d_c\approx 2.43674$, where $d_c$ is determined by two transcendental equations. In the same trajectory class, the system is locally controllable between still-water equilibria if and only if $T>2$. These thresholds confirm Coron's conjecture for steady-state transfer and give a larger value for local exact controllability. The same quadratic endpoint formula and nonlinear correction yield the positive results for both problems. At $T_c$, comparison with a critical plane curve gives the obstruction to local exact controllability. At $T=2$, the nonlinear flux forces small trajectories between still-water equilibria to be stationary.

Optimization and Control.title: Approximate Controllability of the generalized Burgers-Huxley equation in one dimension
Optimization and Control.summary: The generalized Burgers-Huxley (GBH) equation is a prototype model that describes the interplay among reaction, convection, and diffusion. In this article, we explore the controllability of this model by means of an interior control supported in an arbitrary non-empty open subset of the domain. We establish that the GBH equation is not globally approximately controllable in a given time. However, it is possible to steer the system from any steady state to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of another steady state in some suitable time by means of a localized interior control, provided that both steady states lie in the same connected component of the set of steady states.
Optimization and Control.comment: Updated the abstract and literature review in the introduction, and improved the proofs of theorems and propositions. Main results remain unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Finite-Dimensional Internal Stabilization of Steady States of the Gray-Scott System
Optimization and Control.summary: In this article, we establish the local exponential stabilization of every steady state of the Gray-Scott system with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, other than the trivial state $(0,1)^{\top}$, at any prescribed decay rate by finite-dimensional feedback controls supported in an arbitrary nonempty open subset of the domain and acting only on the first equation of the system. Our approach does not require the steady state to be spatially constant and accommodates non-self-adjoint linearizations with variable coefficients. The proof combines unique continuation, a nonvanishing property of the steady-state coupling, the Fattorini-Hautus condition, and Riccati-based feedback.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal isotropic three-material conducting composites with an ideal conductor, in the plane and in space.Bounds and optimal structures
Optimization and Control.summary:
The paper describes an optimal isotropic three-dimensional, three-material conducting composite. One material is an ideal conductor, the volume fractions are prescribed, and the objective is to minimize the effective conductivity over all admissible layouts.
  We first derive a lower bound for the effective conductivity as a function of the material properties and volume fractions. The composite energy is bounded below by a constrained polyconvex envelope, where quadratic and cubic null Lagrangians are imposed through Lagrange multipliers. We further assume that the fields in optimal structures are positive semidefinite. Together with the use of the cubic null Lagrangian, this assumption makes the bound exact. The resulting bound determines the extremal conductivity and the set of associated support fields in optimal structures. Depending on the parameters, it has five regions with different analytic expressions.
  We then prove the bound attainability by constructing optimal structures that realize the bound in every region. They are spherical atoms: a core of the intermediate-conducting material, surrounded by a mantle of wrapped optimal planar structures. In the two extreme regions, a crust is added from the material whose prescribed volume fraction is excessive.

Optimization and Control.title: Ordering error estimates under mesh-uniform regularity and optimal two-mesh design for the KdV equation with boundary dissipation
Optimization and Control.summary: We study Galerkin error estimates and optimal two-mesh design for the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. The ordering error is introduced to measure how much the nonlinearity changes the discretization error. A weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin scheme has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. On a small ball of the energy space, the discrete solution maps are also analytic in the initial datum, with bounds uniform in $h$. On this ball the ordering error is at most of order $h^{1/6}$ times the squared energy norm of the datum, for all $t\ge0$. For $u_0$ on this ball and in the domain $D(A)$ of the linearized generator, the bound is of order $h^2\|u_0\|_{H^3}^{3/2}\|u_0\|_{L^2}^{1/2}$. A two-mesh computation adds a nonlinear correction on a coarse mesh to a linear simulation on a fine mesh. Its error is the linear error on the fine mesh plus the ordering error on the coarse mesh. Based on these error estimates, we formulate a model of the optimal two-mesh design: minimize the cost subject to an accuracy constraint given by the error bounds. For data in a small ball of $L^2$, the problem is convex in logarithmic mesh sizes. When the relative error bound for the coarsest allowed mesh exceeds the prescribed tolerance $η$, the optimal pair and its KKT multipliers are unique. For smooth data the problem is convex in the mesh sizes, and the optimal mesh ratio is independent of the tolerance until the coarse mesh reaches its upper limit. In both cases we characterize the small-amplitude limit of the relative cost when the relative tolerance is proportional to the amplitude.
Optimization and Control.comment: 35 pages, 1 figure. Combines a shortened version of arXiv:2610.39269 (energy-level estimates only) with new results on the optimal design of two-mesh computations. Lean 4 files and computational records in the ancillary files

Optimization and Control.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
Optimization and Control.summary: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.
Optimization and Control.comment: 34 pages, 2 figures. Exact rational Python verifiers and a Lean 4 library for selected lemmas and finite certificates accompany the submission

Optimization and Control.title: Sharp Convergence of Extended Douglas--Rachford Splitting with Variable Relaxation
Optimization and Control.summary: We establish a sharp convergence theory for extended Douglas--Rachford splitting when the first operator is maximally monotone and the second is a convex subdifferential on a real Hilbert space. The resolvent stepsizes may be chosen independently, and the relaxation parameter may depend on the current and past iterates. For fixed stepsizes $α,β>0$, let $\vartheta=\min\{2,2α/β\}$. Assuming the sum of the operators has a zero, we prove weak convergence under $0<θ_k\le\vartheta$ and $\sum_kθ_k(\vartheta-θ_k)=\infty$. Within these pointwise bounds, the divergence condition is also necessary for a universal convergence guarantee when the relaxation sequence is prescribed in advance. Constant relaxation recovers the exact range $0<θ<\vartheta$, resolving a conjecture of Nilsson, Åkerman, and Giselsson. We also establish a sharp bound on growth of the residual, defined as the difference between the two resolvent outputs. We combine this bound with a new Lyapunov function whose definition is independent of the relaxation parameter to obtain a last-iterate residual rate, including $o(N^{-1/2})$ when the relaxation parameters remain uniformly separated from both endpoints.

Optimization and Control.title: Feedback Exact Controllability of the Nonlinear Diffusion Equation with Controller in Coefficients
Optimization and Control.summary: One designs a feedback controller for semilinear parabolic equations with controller in diffusion coefficients which steers the initial data y0 in a given state y1 in a finite time.

Optimization and Control.title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
Optimization and Control.summary: Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning. Additionally, a local-search repair algorithm adapts precomputed B&P or MCS-B&P solutions to demand perturbations through single-flip and per-user trajectory re-optimization, avoiding complete re-optimization. Simulations using realistic large scale constellations, including Starlink Gen-1, demonstrate that MCS-B&P achieves solution quality comparable to exact B&P with fewer column-generation iterations, fewer branch-and-bound nodes, and reduced computation time. HAVD and CAP offer effective online and offline cost-latency trade-offs, while local-search repair recovers most performance losses due to demand perturbations at a fraction of the computational cost of full re-optimization.

Optimization and Control.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
Optimization and Control.summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.

Optimization and Control.title: Construction of Universal Safe Stabilizing Formulas with Weighted Centroid Methodology
Optimization and Control.summary: Control Lyapunov and control barrier functions ensure stability and safety, respectively, by imposing state-dependent affine constraints on the control input. Controller design can therefore be viewed as the problem of selecting an admissible input from the set defined by these constraints. This paper adopts this perspective and develops a weighted-centroid methodology for constructing explicit feedback formulas that are provably smooth. The selection method relies on the fact that weighted centroids of a convex set lie within the set. We establish conditions on the weight functions that guarantee smoothness and continuity for several classes of constraints, including single constraints, mirrored constraints, linearly independent multiple constraints, and two-constraint Gaussian constructions. The framework recovers Sontag's universal formula and generates other new explicit formulas. When specialized to control-theoretic settings, the resulting formulas yield smooth safety filters, stabilizing controllers, and safe-stabilizing controllers. Simulation and hardware experiments on a small quadrotor illustrate the practical benefits of the proposed construction.
Optimization and Control.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control

Optimization and Control.title: Teleoperator-Aware and CBF-Based Adaptive Nonlinear MPC for Shared Autonomy in Obstacle Avoidance of Legged Robots
Optimization and Control.summary: Safe and effective collaboration between humans and autonomous legged robots is a fundamental challenge in shared autonomy, particularly for teleoperated systems navigating cluttered environments. Shared autonomy for legged robots remains challenging due to uncertain human commands, collision-avoidance requirements, and the need to coordinate high-level planning with dynamically feasible locomotion. This paper presents a teleoperator-aware, control barrier function (CBF)-based, adaptive nonlinear model predictive control (ANMPC) framework for shared autonomy of quadrupedal robots in obstacle-avoidance tasks. The framework employs a prescribed arbitration weight between human and robot actions while modeling human inputs using a noisily rational Boltzmann model, whose parameters are adapted online through a projected gradient descent (PGD) law based on observed joystick commands. CBF constraints are incorporated into a computationally efficient NMPC formulation to promote obstacle avoidance while accounting for predicted human actions. The hierarchical architecture integrates high-level CBF-based ANMPC (10 Hz), mid-level dynamics-aware NMPC (60 Hz) enforcing single rigid body (SRB) dynamics, and low-level nonlinear whole-body control (500 Hz). Human-in-the-loop hardware experiments with ten participants on a Unitree Go2 quadruped demonstrate real-time feasibility and collision-free navigation across 50 trials. Shared autonomy reduced average human control effort by 51% and joystick activity from 88% to 42% of trial time, with comparable obstacle clearance and significantly higher perceived assistance than manual operation. Simulation-based ablation studies demonstrate improved obstacle clearance across operator rationality levels and up to a 66% reduction in median human-action prediction error through online adaptation.

Optimization and Control.title: The dimension of optimal plans in multi-marginal optimal transport
Optimization and Control.summary: For general cost functions, we determine the maximal dimension on which solutions to the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with absolutely continuous marginals are concentrated. The dimension is obtained via a novel characteristic integer associated with the Hessian of the cost function. Applications are given to important examples of multi-marginal problems like Wasserstein barycenters, Wasserstein cubic splines and Brenier's generalized Euler equations.

Optimization and Control.title: Mirror Descent at the Edge of Stability
Optimization and Control.summary: In many deep learning settings, gradient descent has been shown to operate at the edge of stability -- a regime where the largest eigenvalue of the loss Hessian hovers around $2/η$. We study this phenomenon in mirror descent, a generalization of gradient descent. As mirror descent is non-Euclidean, existing explanations of the edge of stability phase do not extend to this setting. We generalize the existing notion of sharpness to introduce mirror sharpness, which measures the curvature of the loss with respect to the mirror potential. Empirically, we observe that the mirror sharpness hovers slightly above the $2/η$ threshold. Furthermore, we derive a dual central flow ODE for mirror descent that models iterates in continuous time at the onset of edge of stability. Our ODE provides insights into the difficulties of extending existing arguments for why sharpness stabilizes at $2/η$ from gradient descent to mirror descent in full generality.

Optimization and Control.title: An Exact Penalty Method for Large-Scale Equality-Constrained Nonlinear Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We present an exact penalty method for equality-constrained nonlinear optimization. Our approach transforms the smooth, constrained problem into a sequence of nonsmooth, unconstrained problems by penalizing the constraint violation by its Euclidean norm. An outer loop updates the penalty parameter and the subproblem tolerances, while an inner loop solves each penalized subproblem with a quadratic regularization method. The method also includes a local infeasibility detection mechanism, an extrapolation strategy for warm-starting subproblems, and nonmonotone acceptance rules. We establish global convergence to first-order stationary points under a bounded penalty parameter assumption, with a worst-case complexity of \(\mathcal{O}(|\log ε|\,ε^{-2})\) inner iterations. We implement the method in Penelopt, an open-source Julia solver for constrained nonlinear optimization. On \(224\) problems from the CUTEst collection, Penelopt is competitive with IPOPT and more robust than the recent solvers MadNLP and Uno. These results establish exact penalty methods as a practical alternative to conventional methods for solving equality-constrained nonlinear optimization problems. To the best of our knowledge, Penelopt is the first practical implementation of an exact penalty method for large-scale constrained nonlinear optimization.

Optimization and Control.title: Parallel batch scheduling for optimizing hospital sterilization operations: arc-flow formulations, column generation and Lagrangian heuristics for flowtime minimization
Optimization and Control.summary: In a recent work by Schlembach et al., the problem of optimally managing sterilization operations in hospitals has been modeled as a machine scheduling problem with parallel batch processing and minimum flowtime objective, and heuristically solved by column generation. We draw upon this approach, developing arc-flow formulations and related column-generation procedures, using an exact dynamic programming algorithm to solve the pricing problems. We further derive Lagrangian relaxations based on minimum cost flows and shortest paths, with subgradient optimization and the volume algorithm guiding batch generation. A makespan bound for schedules minimizing total flow time provides a finite horizon when no operational limit is known. Computational experiments on literature benchmarks and more challenging generated instances demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. The arc-flow model solves all literature benchmark instances to proven optimality within seconds, while the Lagrangian heuristics deliver high-quality schedules with substantially reduced computational effort.
Optimization and Control.comment: Submitted to European Journal of Operational Research

Optimization and Control.title: Average-reward reinforcement learning in semi-Markov decision processes via relative value iteration
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper applies the authors' recent results on asynchronous stochastic approximation (SA) in the Borkar-Meyn framework to reinforcement learning in average-reward semi-Markov decision processes (SMDPs). We establish the convergence of an asynchronous SA analogue of Schweitzer's classical relative value iteration algorithm, RVI Q-learning, for finite-space, weakly communicating SMDPs. In particular, we show that the algorithm converges almost surely to a compact, connected subset of solutions to the average-reward optimality equation, with convergence to a unique, sample path-dependent solution under additional stepsize and asynchrony conditions. Moreover, to make full use of the SA framework, we introduce new monotonicity conditions for estimating the optimal reward rate in RVI Q-learning. These conditions substantially expand the previously considered algorithmic framework and are addressed through novel arguments in the stability and convergence analysis of RVI Q-learning.
Optimization and Control.comment: 26 pages. This paper presents the reinforcement-learning material previously contained in version 2 of arXiv:2409.03915, which was subsequently split into two stand-alone papers. This update adds several examples and discussions, along with minor clarifications and editorial changes. The main technical content remains unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Structured Adaptive Tensor Prediction for Streaming Data
Optimization and Control.summary: Matrix-valued time series arise in a wide range of applications, such as spatio-temporal data in medical imaging and geophysics. Existing forecasting methods are mainly designed for static settings, while adaptive filtering techniques have been largely limited to scalar- or vector-valued data. In this paper, we develop an adaptive tensor prediction framework for streaming matrix-valued data based on a Tensor-on-Matrix (ToM) regression model, in which the responses in a sliding window are lifted to a third-order tensor and the regression tensor is updated online by stochastic gradient descent (SGD). We derive the leading terms of the steady-state and tracking errors of SGD with overlapping windows, which show that the steady-state error is proportional to the step size and the noise variance, and that the step size governs a trade-off between noise and tracking. We further analyze the statistical accuracy of structured ToM regression within a single window. We establish a restricted isometry property, which holds when the window length is proportional to the input dimension, and derive recovery error bounds for sparse, low-rank and sparse plus low-rank regression tensors, which show that the recovery error scales with the intrinsic degrees of freedom rather than the ambient dimension. Simulations confirm the theoretical results, and the effectiveness of the structured adaptive updates is validated on the tracking of a drifting quantum gate, citywide crowd-flow prediction, and global total electron content (TEC) forecasting.

Optimization and Control.title: Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers
Optimization and Control.summary: Deep unfolding (DU) accelerates iterative optimizers by training learnable components through unrolled iterations, but extending DU to the large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) common in robotics has remained limited. Unrolling a full-update conic solver such as COSMO exposes two obstacles: backpropagating through the per-iteration linear-system solve incurs memory quadratic in the problem size when the coefficient matrix is formed explicitly, and backpropagating through the positive semidefinite (PSD) cone projection is numerically unstable under repeated eigenvalues. We address the first with a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule that reduces memory from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n + \mathrm{nnz}(A))$, and the second with a stable backward rule based on the Dalečkii--Krein representation of the Fréchet derivative. Together, these enable learning lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm starts for COSMO. On standalone SDPs and second-order cone programs, ranging from max-cut and Lovász $\vartheta$ to robust estimation and control, the learned policies outperform tuned COSMO on every problem class, reducing iterations to tolerance by up to 60$\times$, and transfer without retraining to instances up to 10$\times$ larger in the size parameter while retaining 2--5$\times$ speedups. Our matrix-free solver implementation also batches naturally on the GPU, solving 64 Lovász $\vartheta$ SDPs 14$\times$ faster than sequential COSMO. When embedded in sequential convex programming for nonlinear covariance steering, our learned optimizers outperform the interior-point solver Clarabel in terms of both success rate and solve time.

Optimization and Control.title: Robust Pair--Restricted Lipschitz Regression with Global--Local Transfer
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop a robust pair-restricted Lipschitz regression framework for grouped longitudinal data represented as finite trajectories in a space equipped with a prescribed or learned pseudometric. For a fixed geometry, latent responses and a Lipschitz bound are estimated jointly through a convex optimisation problem with constraints imposed on selected trajectory pairs. We show that the choice of fidelity loss leads to different structural behaviour: Huber regularisation strictly reduces the pair-restricted Lipschitz seminorm whenever the exact interpolant has a finite positive seminorm, whereas $L^1$ fidelity can preserve exact interpolation below a data-dependent threshold. For grouped observations, global and local Lipschitz structures are combined while keeping group identity outside the trajectory geometry. The global component draws on observations from other groups, while the local component uses each group's history to account for group-specific behaviour. We also characterise when group-specific observations can be fitted exactly under a shared Lipschitz bound and establish a regularity bound for the combined predictor. We describe a computational implementation based on constraint generation and illustrate the framework through an application to longitudinal sow-production data.

Optimization and Control.title: Conjugate continuous-discrete projection filter via sparse-Grid quadrature
Optimization and Control.summary: In this article, we study the continuous-discrete projection filter for exponential-family manifolds with conjugate likelihoods. We first derive the local projection error of the prediction step of the continuous-discrete projection filter. We then derive the exact Bayesian update algorithm for a class of discrete measurement processes with additive Gaussian noise. To control the stiffness of the natural parameters' ordinary differential equations, we introduce a regularization method via projection to the Fisher information metric's eigenspace. Lastly, we apply the proposed method to approximate the filtering density of a modified Van der Pol oscillator problem and a coupled stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo system. The proposed projection filter shows superior performance compared to several state-of-the-art parametric continuous-discrete filtering methods.

Optimization and Control.title: A feasible point method for derivative-free linearly constrained optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper presents a framework for linearly constrained derivative-free optimization (DFO) in which the original objective function is evaluated only at feasible points. The method first analyzes the linear constraint system using certificates of infeasibility and implied activity to detect infeasibility or a singleton feasible set, or, when the feasible set has positive dimension, to identify the affine subspace spanned by the feasible set and obtain an equivalent reduced representation with a strictly feasible base point. It then transforms the resulting reduced problem into an unconstrained optimization problem by means of a pointed feasible retraction and an exact penalty function. The retraction maps arbitrary trial points to feasible points by an explicit scaling in the reduced coordinates, so that no constrained optimization or projection subproblem is required during objective evaluations. This construction permits a broad range of unconstrained DFO methods to be used as inner solvers while preserving feasibility of the original objective evaluations. Numerical experiments compare several such variants on linearly constrained test problems of different dimensions. The results show that the choice of inner solver affects robustness, the number of problems solved, function-evaluation efficiency, and computational time, and that relative performance changes with problem dimension.

Optimization and Control.title: OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
Optimization and Control.summary: Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. At student-generated prefixes, we form a four-observation matrix by treating the student and teacher as both candidate sources and evaluators. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/OC-OPD.

Optimization and Control.title: Convergence of Large-Stepsize SGD for the Cross-entropy Loss via Stochastic Lyapunov Stability
Optimization and Control.summary: Modern deep learning has been shown to operate using learning rates far larger than those justified by classical optimization theory. Most prior analyses of this phenomenon focus on deterministic gradient descent, leaving the stochastic setting largely unexplored. In this work, we provide sharp convergence guarantees for Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) applied to the multiclass cross-entropy loss, for both linear classifiers and two-layer neural networks. We show that the stochasticity of SGD may cause the dynamics to alternate between an edge-of-stability regime that is dominated by curvature-driven oscillations, and a stable regime in which the expected loss decreases at a controlled rate. Despite that, we prove that SGD stabilizes the dynamics, ensuring that the iterates return to stability in a fixed number of iterations and allowing convergence in the best-iterate sense even with large learning rates. Experiments validate our theoretical findings and illustrate the benefits of SGD in the large-stepsize regime.

Optimization and Control.title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
Optimization and Control.summary: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

Optimization and Control.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
Optimization and Control.summary: Data-driven model predictive control based on Koopman operator theory is a promising approach for constrained control of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control framework for such systems using bilinear Koopman realizations with state- and input-dependent proportional approximation-error bounds that vanish at the target equilibrium. Since prediction in lifted coordinates with a finite-dimensional Koopman realization need not remain on the manifold of valid lifted states, multi-step prediction may leave the region where one-step error certificates apply. We avoid this difficulty by reprojecting each predicted lifted state onto the original state coordinates and lifting it again, yielding an error-aware discrete-time control-affine predictor in the original state space without assuming invariance of the Koopman dictionary. For this predictor, we develop a homothetic tube construction based on a discrete-time robust control contraction metric whose radius explicitly accounts for the proportional approximation error bounds. The tube tightening handles arbitrary continuously differentiable nonlinear constraints, and the resulting model predictive control problem includes terminal ingredients and a tube-radius penalty that exploits the vanishing uncertainty near the target. We prove robust satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, recursive feasibility, and exponential stability of the sampled true closed-loop system with high probability over the training data without requiring a globally optimal solution to the model predictive control problem. Numerical examples, including nonlinear obstacle-avoidance constraints, demonstrate robust stabilization and higher performance of the proposed approach compared to existing Koopman-based model predictive control methods in terms of smaller closed-loop cost and flexibility.

Optimization and Control.title: A Wasserstein Trust-Region Method for Smooth Potential-Interaction Energies
Optimization and Control.summary:
Finding low-energy particle configurations and approximating probability distributions both lead to minimizing potential-interaction energies in Wasserstein space. Second-order information can speed up minimizing these possibly nonconvex energies, but a quadratic model is accurate only near the current measure. We introduce a Wasserstein trust-region (WTR) method for smooth, possibly nonconvex energies of this type. Each iteration transports the current measure $ρ$ along a displacement field $s$, producing $(\mathrm{Id}+s)_\#ρ$. The field approximately minimizes a quadratic model built from the second variation of the energy, subject to $\|s\|_{L^2(ρ)}\leΔ$, using a truncated conjugate-gradient method. The ratio of actual to predicted decrease determines step acceptance and updates the trust-region radius.
  Under a lower energy bound and globally bounded Hessians of the potential and interaction kernel, we prove that the objective is nonincreasing, the Wasserstein-gradient norms converge to zero, and an $\varepsilon$-stationary iterate is reached within $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations, rejected ones included. If the potential is quadratically coercive, every weak accumulation point is stationary. For empirical measures, WTR is an ordinary trust-region method in the particle positions, and its complexity bound does not depend on the number of particles provided the initial energy exceeds its infimum by a bounded amount. For $2048$ and $4096$ particles with Gaussian pair repulsion in a two-dimensional harmonic trap, WTR reaches the gradient tolerance $2\times10^{-4}$ a median $1.40$ times faster than L-BFGS. For equal-weight integration rules on two non-Gaussian targets, WTR reaches an integration error of $10^{-4}$ about $1.8$ times faster than L-BFGS and $1.3$ times faster than a Krylov trust-region solver.

Optimization and Control.title: Localisation for the second-order Beckmann problem: bimartingale couplings and leaf decompositions
Optimization and Control.summary:
We develop a second-order localisation theory for optimal transport based on leaf decompositions and bimartingale couplings, which impose martingale constraints in opposite directions on complementary orthogonal subspaces. It provides a second-order analogue of the classical decomposition of optimal transport into transport rays and monotone couplings: transport rays are replaced by the leaves of the $1$-Lipschitz derivative map $Du$ of an optimal dual potential $u\in C^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$, while monotone couplings are replaced by bimartingale couplings.
  We apply this framework to the three-marginal optimal transport problem introduced by Bolbotowski and Bouchitté, whose relaxation is the second-order Beckmann problem.
  We characterise the existence of bimartingale couplings through a convex-concave order condition. This yields a generalisation of Strassen's theorem from convex order to the convex-concave setting. Equivalently, the dual problem associated with the second-order Beckmann problem admits an optimiser whose derivative is an isometry.
  For absolutely continuous measures with common barycentre, assuming the existence of an optimal plan with absolutely continuous third marginal, we prove that every optimal plan decomposes into a family of problems on the leaves of $Du$. On each leaf, all optimal plans are completely described by bimartingale couplings between the corresponding conditional measures.
  Without this absolute continuity assumption on the third marginal, we show that the leaf decomposition persists in a more general form: optimal plans are mixtures of plans concentrated on triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $x\in \mathcal{S}_1$, $y\in \mathcal{S}_2$, and $z\in \mathcal{S}_1\cap \mathcal{S}_2$, where $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are neighbouring leaves of $Du$.
Optimization and Control.comment: 53 pages, 3 figures; version accepted in the Calculus of Variations and Partial Differential Equations; comments are welcome

Optimization and Control.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Sample Complexity of Natural Policy Gradient with a Matching Information-Theoretic Lower Bound
Optimization and Control.summary: A fundamental question in reinforcement learning is how many sampled transitions are needed to learn a near-optimal policy, and whether direct policy optimization can attain this statistical limit. To answer this question, we consider natural policy gradient (NPG), a widely used policy optimization method. We study tabular finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) with known rewards and unknown horizon-dependent transition kernels, accessed through a generative model. Our sample-based NPG algorithms update the policy by backward sweeps and do not estimate transition probabilities. Under three different batch-size and step size schedules, we establish last-iterate guarantees with sample complexity $\widetilde O(SAH^4/\varepsilon^2)$, where $S$, $A$, and $H$ denote the number of states, the number of actions, and the horizon length, respectively. In this setting, horizon-dependent transition kernels contribute a factor of $H$ to our transition-query bound. Our information-theoretic lower bound of $Ω(SAH^4/\varepsilon^2)$ shows that the resulting $H^4$ dependence is unavoidable in the worst case, even for agents that select their queries adaptively. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first last-iterate guarantees for NPG whose sample complexity matches an information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Consequently, our results demonstrate that direct policy-space optimization through NPG can achieve the fundamental statistical limits of reinforcement learning while guaranteeing the performance of the final policy. Furthermore, for known kernels, we prove that exact NPG with a constant step size $η=1/H$ requires $Ω(H^2/\varepsilon)$ iterations in the worst case, matching the known upper bound for that step size.

Optimization and Control.title: Neural Schrödinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a novel neural solver for inferring the continuous state evolution of the Schrödinger bridge problem. The proposed solver builds on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. This allows us to realize the continuous state evolution by learning the optimal velocity for an ordinary differential equation, as opposed to learning the optimal drift for a stochastic differential equation. The proposed solver only uses the source and the target samples, and not the source and target distributions per se, which makes it particularly suitable for high dimensional applications arising in generative modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solver using several numerical experiments in low and high dimensions, using both real and synthetic datasets.

Optimization and Control.title: Dynamic Programming without Contractivity
Optimization and Control.summary: Optimality results in dynamic programming are usually derived from contraction arguments, which require discounting or uniform bounds on termination times. We show that, in many useful settings, contractivity can be replaced by a simple global stability condition that requires no rate or uniformity. Under this condition and mild order-theoretic assumptions, we obtain existence of optimal policies, uniqueness of the value function as a solution to the Bellman equation, and convergence of value function iteration and of Howard and optimistic policy iteration. Applications include optimal stopping without discounting, where contraction methods can fail, and Bayesian sequential analysis.

Optimization and Control.title: Multi-location Newsvendor: An Interpretable Inventory Policy
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a multilocation newsvendor problem in which inventory is chosen before demand is observed and surplus stock can subsequently be transshipped to locations with shortages. The objective is to minimize expected holding, backlog, and transportation costs over a metric network. Under uniform transportation costs, the optimality conditions balance local and aggregate demand coverage and reduce to a scalar search under mild regularity conditions. We use this structure to develop an interpretable iterative heuristic for general metrics. The heuristic calibrates effective transportation costs from lateral shipments under independent stocking and uses them to construct location-dependent pooling weights. These weights have a direct operational interpretation through the cost of serving demand at other locations. Under the stated assumptions, the heuristic recovers the exact uniform-metric solution. Numerical experiments on structured and random networks show costs close to the sampled optimum on average and substantial savings relative to independent stocking.

Optimization and Control.title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
Optimization and Control.summary: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chvátal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture. We give a totally half-modular $5\times6$ matrix that does not have the Edmonds-Johnson property and has no minor equal to either matrix. It is a minimal obstruction: every proper minor has the Edmonds-Johnson property. The proofs work on a graph whose edges are the rows and bounds of the matrix, and on which the minor operations act by deleting, contracting and halving edges. For minimality, we reduce every proper minor to two classes of matrices known to have the Edmonds-Johnson property.

Optimization and Control.title: An ADMM-Based Approach to the Large-Scale Geomagnetically Induced Current Blocker Placement Problem
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based approach for addressing the challenge of determining placements for geomagnetically induced current (GIC) blocking devices on large-scale transmission networks. Traditional formulations of this placement problem lead to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) that are difficult for state-of-the-art MINLP solvers, which often struggle to exploit problem structure and fail to produce high-quality solutions on large systems. To overcome these challenges, the proposed method employs a three-block ADMM decomposition enhanced with (i) partial linearization of the GIC-related nonlinearities, supported by conditions guaranteeing exactness, and (ii) heterogeneous penalty parameters that significantly accelerate convergence to high-quality local solutions. Numerical experiments on newly constructed large-scale benchmark systems (up to 10,000 buses) demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods by several orders of magnitude in runtime while producing solutions whose objective values closely approach the ideal all-blocker lower bound. These results highlight the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach for mitigation planning efforts in large transmission networks.

Optimization and Control.title: Jointly Recovering Destination Attractiveness and Spatial Preference Segments from Observed Tours via Inverse Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Quantifying destination attractiveness by counting visitors, the most direct approach, can favor accessible sites and understate destinations that travelers reach at considerable cost. Preferences may also cut across a priori socio-demographic groupings. This study develops an inverse optimization framework that recovers destination attractiveness and preference segments jointly from observed multi-stop trip tours and generalized travel costs, without prespecifying tour-level segment assignments or imposing a parametric distribution on the unexplained part of utility. Representing each destination visit as a link in an extended network turns utility-maximizing tour choice into an inverse shortest paths problem. We apply the framework to 2,931 holiday vehicle trip tours over 51 target municipalities in Hokkaido, Japan. Constraint generation and alternating optimization make estimation tractable in this multi-destination setting, and the segments recovered under a three-segment specification show contrasting spatial preferences across the established coastal centers, the corridor around Sapporo, and the inland lake districts. The recovered values are expressed on a common monetary scale across destinations and segments without segment-specific scale normalization. They are uncorrelated with visit counts in the input data (r = -0.01) yet moderately correlated with tourist arrivals from an independent prefectural survey (r = 0.40), and are positively associated with the cost of reaching a destination (r = 0.60); destinations above this cost-value relationship include niche places that visit counts alone do not distinguish. The results provide a spatially explicit account of destination value and preference heterogeneity that can inform urban and regional planning and segment-targeted marketing.

Optimization and Control.title: Data-driven discovery of sparse governing equations with parameterized operators
Optimization and Control.summary: We study parameterized SINDy (pSINDy), an extension of the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) framework for the discovery of parsimonious governing equations involving operators with unknown parameters such as fractional-order Caputo derivatives, fractional Laplacians, and parameterized kernel operators. The framework jointly identifies the unknown operator parameters and sparse library coefficients through a sparsity-promoting optimization problem. To solve this problem, we develop and analyze the parameterized sequentially thresholded least-squares (pSTLSQ) algorithm. In each iteration, it removes terms with small coefficients, updates the operator parameters by a fixed number of optimization steps that improve the fit of the remaining library terms, and refits their coefficients by least squares. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that pSTLSQ converges locally to a local minimizer and give sufficient conditions for identifying the terms present in the governing equation. Numerical experiments demonstrate recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data for fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal diffusion equations. We also examine the influence of the hyperparameters, discretization scheme, and noise, and compare pSTLSQ with two benchmark methods. All three methods identify the correct terms at low noise levels, but differ in parameter accuracy, cost, and sensitivity to initialization and the candidate library.

Optimization and Control.title: Mechanism Design under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility and Rent Capacity
Optimization and Control.summary: A seller jointly chooses allocation and payments when buyers misperceive competition. Under independent private values, statewise participation, and payment restrictions, allocation determines both required rents and their delivery capacity. We separate these effects under a common subjective law. For three values and shared-top beliefs, explicit score and capacity conditions characterize globally optimal lower-value lotteries, including top-rent overflow and welfare differences among revenue optima. A two-buyer construction establishes a strict allocation advantage over every reserve under the same fixed reporting certificate and positive margin. A transport test and exact band-boundary incentive equalities identify separate conditions restoring objective-law revenue ceilings. For three bands and a common affine belief interval, an explicitly certified reserve attains the ceiling under stated score conditions. A case scaled to public collectible-auction records yields a nominal shared-top allocation gain of 24.72 cents per auction. A one-cent report-by-report margin yields matched gains of 1.48 cents under projection and 3.32 cents under shared-top beliefs; the three-band point-belief gain of 2.50 cents disappears with common-interval protection. These comparisons bound the additional recurring costs an allocation redesign can cover at the specified reporting requirement.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal User-Level Private Stochastic Convex Optimization and Mean Estimation with Heavy Tails
Optimization and Control.summary: We study stochastic convex optimization with heavy-tailed stochastic gradients under $(\varepsilon, δ)$-user-level differential privacy, which protects each user's entire collection of samples. Instead of assuming a uniformly bounded Lipschitz constant, we only assume bounds on the second- and $k$-th moments of the random sample Lipschitz parameters. This allows for unbounded, heavy-tailed stochastic gradient distributions and can lead to sharper excess risk bounds. We characterize the minimax optimal excess population risk up to logarithmic factors. Our algorithm achieves the optimal rate with only $\widetilde{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ users. As a byproduct of our algorithmic developments, we obtain tight bounds for user-level private mean estimation under norm-moment assumptions, improving over the guarantees of Esfandiari et al. (2022) and Zhao et al. (2024). Finally, for mean estimation under the directional-moment assumption of Agarwal et al. (2025), we close their remaining approximate-DP gap by removing the additional $d/\varepsilon$ user requirement and attaining the optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

Optimization and Control.title: A Generalized Framework for Structured Low-Rank Approximation and Completion
Optimization and Control.summary: We formulate a generalized version of SLRA, consisting of general affine constraints, which subsumes the problems of structured low-rank matrix approximation and completion as special cases. We characterize its critical points and propose an algorithm to approximately solve the general problem. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm for stock-price forecasting, computing approximate gcd of polynomials with noisy coefficients, and time-series denoising.

Optimization and Control.title: Sub-Riemannian flow matching
Optimization and Control.summary: We study sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching (SRCFM) for generative transport with prescribed velocity constraints. Training uses paths between sampled source and target points whose velocities lie in the allowed horizontal directions at each state. A neural network takes time and the full state as input and predicts the coefficients of these directions, and the horizontal frame then determines the full velocity used for generation. We describe constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and joint endpoint equations in free step-two Carnot groups. We propose a scalable piecewise algorithm that computes horizontal paths directly from their endpoints. A straight segment sets the horizontal coordinates, and a loop in those coordinates corrects the remaining vertical displacement. We verify the algorithm's endpoint accuracy to numerical precision in high-dimensional tests. Synthetic experiments illustrate approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories. On resized MNIST, we use the same construction to generate images from Gaussian inputs with fewer controls than pixels.

Optimization and Control.title: A Unified Bregman Projection Framework for Solving Multi-Split Multiple-Set Implicit Convex Feasibility Problems
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the multi-split multiple-set implicit convex feasibility problem (MSMS-ICFP), in which the constraint sets are generated by point-to-set operators and the feasibility conditions are imposed both in the original space and in several image spaces connected by bounded linear operators. We analyze the generalized proximity function, built from weighted Bregman distances and Bregman projections, introduced by Censor and Dey. For translation-type point-to-set operators, we establish the continuity and Lipschitz continuity of the corresponding Bregman projections, the continuous differentiability of the proximity function with an explicit formula for its gradient, and global and local Lipschitz estimates for this gradient. We then propose a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm. In the nonconvex case, the gradient norms of the iterates converge to zero and every accumulation point is stationary. When the proximity function is convex and the solution set is nonempty, the iterates converge in norm to a solution, with an $O(1/k)$ rate for the proximity values, an $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ rate for the gradient norms, and a linear rate under a quadratic growth condition. Cyclic and block-iterative variants are also analyzed. Numerical experiments, including a cooperative sensor network localization problem, illustrate the theory and show that, in contrast with frozen-set implicit projection methods, the proposed gradient schemes remain convergent when the translation operators are expansive.

Optimization and Control.title: A Lower Bound on the Sliced Wasserstein Comparison Constant for Translated Measures
Optimization and Control.summary: We provide closed-form expressions for standard 1-Wasserstein distance ($W_1$) and Sliced 1-Wasserstein distance ($SW_1$) for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Furthermore, we construct an explicit lower bound for the constant $c_d$ established by Carlier, Figalli, Mérigot, and Wang between $W_1$ and $SW_1$ [1] for translated probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Sliced Wasserstein distances are computationally efficient and used in image generation and other applications, which raises natural questions in computational efficiency versus theoretical correctness. A lower bound on the constant $c_d$ gives information about the cost of that efficiency.
Optimization and Control.comment: 2nd version: extended Propositions 1 & 2 to finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, fixed typos and added acknowledgments

Optimization and Control.title: Pooled Inverse Optimization: Learning the Unique Optimal Decision from Repeated Observations
Optimization and Control.summary: Inverse optimization infers a decision-maker's objective from observed decisions. We study repeated noisy observations of one decision. Classical formulations impute a separate optimum for each observation, so their size grows with the sample, and may return one of many equally compatible objectives. With a bounded polyhedral feasible set and a cost vector drawn from a distribution with a density, the optimum is almost surely a unique vertex. Its compatible costs form a full-dimensional cone that repeated observations of the same decision cannot shrink. Pooled inverse optimization fits one optimum to all observations and reports its compatible cost cone. Under squared loss, the optimization model has fixed size after aggregation, the decision estimate has a finite-sample error bound, and guarded rounding recovers the true vertex and its full cone with probability tending to one. A single convex program sufficed in every linear scaling run. With 50 variables and 10,000 observations, median runtimes were 8 milliseconds under squared loss and 8 seconds under absolute loss. The standard mixed-integer formulation reached its time limit at 100 observations. At 10,000 observations, the remaining two exact formulations under absolute loss and two convex baselines reached their 10- to 60-minute limits. Using national survey data on women with hypertension and diabetes or prediabetes, the method finds in milliseconds the diet closest to each woman's mean reported intake subject to DASH-based nutrient bounds in a food-group model and identifies which bounds bind.
Optimization and Control.comment: 35 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Substantially revised and retitled. Previous title: "From Non-Identifiability to Goal-Integrated Decision-Making in Parametric Inverse Optimization". This version treats the pooled model and its computational study; the goal-integrated models of version 1 are not included

Optimization and Control.title: Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.

Optimization and Control.title: Sharp Last-Iterate Bounds for the Stochastic subGradient Method
Optimization and Control.summary: We determine the worst-case expected optimization error of the last iterate of constant-stepsize projected Stochastic subGradient Method on convex Lipschitz objectives. The upper and lower bounds match up to universal constants for every stepsize, horizon, dimension, and conditional noise moment of order $p\in[1,\infty]$. With bounded noise and a fixed positive bound on the initial distance to a minimizer, the best constant stepsize gives worst-case error after $n$ iterates of order $1/\sqrt n$ on the line and $\sqrt{\log n/(n\log\log n)}$ in every fixed dimension at least two.

Optimization and Control.title: Rates of metastability for a generalization of the Halpern iteration
Optimization and Control.summary: We apply proof mining methods developed by Kohlenbach and the second author to compute uniform rates of metastability for a generalization of the Halpern iteration studied by Kanzow and Shehu. As special cases, we obtain rates of metastability for the Halpern and modified Halpern iterations, as well as for the Tikhonov-Mann iteration. Furthermore, convergence results are obtained as immediate consequences of our quantitative results.

Optimization and Control.title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
Optimization and Control.summary: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.

Optimization and Control.title: KL-Guided Support Selection and Subspace Cubic Newton Methods for Sparse Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study sparse composite optimization with a smooth loss and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth regularizer. The objective is locally smooth on each fixed support. Our method combines full-space proximal-gradient steps with inexact cubic-regularized Newton steps on a subspace selected by thresholding. If the iterates are bounded and the objective satisfies the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property, the entire sequence converges to a first-order stationary point. A threshold based on the KL exponent ensures that the selected coordinate set coincides with the support of the limit after finitely many iterations, without requiring a nondegeneracy assumption. We also provide a residual-based threshold when such an exponent exists and its value is unknown. Under an additional continuity assumption on the restricted Hessian, the line search eventually accepts full cubic steps. With bounded cubic regularization parameters and damping parameters chosen to meet the target tolerances, we bound the number of outer iterations needed to reach restricted approximate second-order stationarity after support identification and entry into the full-step regime. We conduct numerical experiments in two settings: when the KL exponent is known and when it is unknown. In the former case, we use a degenerate problem to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. In the latter case, we compare the proposed method and its adaptive variant with existing solvers on sparse recovery and logistic regression problems.

Optimization and Control.title: Stochastic Extragradient Methods Beyond Lipschitz Continuity
Optimization and Control.summary: Stochastic variational inequality problems have received significant attention due to their ability to model large-scale machine learning tasks. Typically, the operators involved are assumed to be globally Lipschitz, with only a handful of works extending beyond the standard setting to the so-called $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz setting. In this work, we propose a novel stochastic past extragradient algorithm for variational inequality problems under a broad regularity assumption that is even less restrictive than $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz continuity and provide convergence guarantees under bounded variance of the stochastic oracle. More precisely, we show a.s. convergence with suitable stepsize schedules and obtain convergence rates in expectation and in probability for fixed horizons. Finally, in numerical simulations we compare our proposed algorithm against standard methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Pseudo-random Instance Generators in C++ for Deterministic and Stochastic Multi-commodity Network Design Problems
Optimization and Control.summary: Network design problems constitute an important family of combinatorial optimization problems for which many exact and heuristic algorithms have been developed over the last few decades. Two central problems in this family are the multi-commodity, capacitated, fixed charge network design problem (MCFNDP) and its stochastic counterpart, the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP with recourse. These are standard problems that often serve as workbenches for devising and testing models and algorithms in stylized but near-realistic settings. Progress on solution methods requires instances of varying size, structure and difficulty. We present two open-source C++ generators. The deterministic generator modernizes and extends the generator underlying the Canad instances, with new topologies and continuous control of capacity tightness and cost structure. The stochastic generator, which is to our knowledge the first publicly available one for the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP, builds scenarios that match user-specified moments and correlations. We also release libraries of configurations for 6,000 deterministic and 416 stochastic instances, as well as the base instances and configurations of 20 stochastic instances on hub-and-spoke benchmark networks. The generators aim to support systematic and reproducible experimentation, including the training and out-of-sample evaluation of learning-based and stochastic programming methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Distributed Optimization of $M$-Convex Functions Subject to Linear Constraints via Continuous Relaxation and Shapley-Folkman Decomposition
Optimization and Control.summary: $M$-convex functions from discrete convex analysis admit tractable minimization and convex extensions that agree with them at integer points. We study the minimization of a separable collection of $N$ $M$-convex functions subject to $m$ linear coupling constraints. Our two-stage algorithm first solves the convex relaxation and then reconstructs an integer solution through local Carathéodory decompositions and an LP purification step. The returned solution has no objective increase relative to the convex-relaxation value and a coupling residual that is $O(m)$ for bounded coupling coefficients, with no explicit dependence on $N$. We prove polynomial value-oracle evaluation of the $M$-convex extension and give both an exact value-oracle-polynomial implementation and a distributed consensus-ADMM implementation under a proximal oracle. We also establish proximity and additive envelope-gap guarantees when Stage~1 uses a strongly convex extension. On an inventory placement problem with up to about $10^6$ products, both guarantees hold on every run, and the method is faster than exact integer-programming benchmarks by a factor that grows with the number of regions.

Optimization and Control.title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method for Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization with Applications
Optimization and Control.summary: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an $O(T^{-1/2})$ best-residual bound holds over $T$ accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.

Optimization and Control.title: Applicability of the MPCC approach to Zeng reformulations of nonlinear pessimistic bilevel programming
Optimization and Control.summary: The vanilla method in bilevel programming is to reformulate it as a single-level mathematical programs with complementarity constraints (MPCC), via the KKT conditions of the lower-level. This method seemed to work only for optimistic formulations. However, in (Zeng, 2020), B. Zeng presented a general method to reduce pessimistic bilevel problems to optimistic ones.
